{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Uesugi Shrine | image = [[File:Uesugi shrine 1.jpg|250px|]]
main hall | location = 1-4-13 Marunouchi, Yonezawa City, [[Yamagata Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|37|54|33.5|N|140|6|14.7|E|region:JP-06_scale:25000_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Uesugi Shrine}} | festival Deities = Lord [[Uesugi Kenshin]] | Shrine rank = Bekkaku Kanpeisha | established = Meiji 4 (1871) | festival = April 29 | deity = [[Uesugi Kenshin]] | Religious ceremony = | map = {{location map|Japan Yonezawa city#Japan Yamagata|label=Uesugi Shrine|position=center|width=200|float=center}} }} [[File:Uesugi kenshin.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Kenshin]] [[File:Uesugi-Yozan statue.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Yozan (located along the approach)]] '''Uesugi Shrine''' (うえすぎじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Yonezawa City]], [[Yamagata Prefecture]]. It is situated in [[Matsugasaki Park]] (the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]]) and enshrines [[Uesugi Kenshin]]. The former shrine rank was [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. It is one of the shrines that enshrine clan founders, which became popular from the late [[Edo period]] to the early [[Meiji period]]. Uesugi Shrine (上杉神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Yonezawa, Yamagata]].{{Cite web|last=Organization|first=Japan National Tourism|title=Uesugi-jinja Shrine {{!}} Travel Japan (Japan National Tourism Organization)|url=https://www.japan.travel/en/spot/434/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=Travel Japan|language=en-us}}{{Cite web|last=山形県観光物産協会|first=公益社団法人|title=Uesugi Jinja Shrine｜What to See & Do｜STAY YAMAGATA|url=https://yamagatakanko.com/en/attractions/detail_1390.html|access-date=2023-04-07|website=STAY YAMAGATA|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=TOKYO|first=COPYRIGHT © TOHOKU ×|title=Uesugi-Jinja Shrine {{!}} TOHOKU x TOKYO (JAPAN)|url=https://www.tohokuandtokyo.org/spot_131/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=www.tohokuandtokyo.org|language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo shrine]] and is dedicated to the memory of [[Uesugi Kenshin]], a famous military leader in Japanese history. The shrine was built in 1876 on the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]], and it enshrines the spirit of [[Uesugi Kenshin]]. Every year in February, a snow lantern festival is held at the shrine where lanterns are carved out of snow to honor the memory of Uesugi Kenshin. It is a popular event that attracts many visitors. ==History== When [[Uesugi Kenshin]] suddenly died in [[Tensho]] 6 (1578) at [[Kasugayama Castle]] in [[Echigo Province]], his remains were enshrined in a Buddhist manner at the Fushikian within the castle. However, when [[Uesugi Kagekatsu]] was transferred to [[Aizu Domain]] and later to [[Yonezawa]] in [[Keicho]] 6 (1601), Kenshin's shrine was also moved to Yonezawa. After that, eleven temples, with [[Ho-onji Temple]] as the chief temple, alternated in conducting the rites at the second bailey of Yonezawa Castle. However, in the Meiji period, due to the [[Shinbutsu Bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and the [[Haijo-rei]] (abolition of castles decree), Kenshin's remains were moved from the castle to the [[Uesugi family mausoleum]], and Ho-onji Temple was relocated in front of the mausoleum for its protection. Additionally, to enshrine Kenshin's spirit in a Shinto manner, a monk from Daijoji Temple, the second of the eleven temples, renounced the monkhood and became a Shinto priest. The priest adopted the surname Daijoji and the family continues to serve as the chief priest to this day. At the same time, the shrine also enshrined [[Uesugi Yozan]], a notable lord who revived the Yonezawa Domain, and it became "Uesugi Shrine" in Yamagata Prefecture. On May 21, Meiji 9 (1876), the shrine building was relocated to its current location, the former inner palace site of Yonezawa Castle. On April 26, Meiji 35 (1902), it was ranked as a [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. At this time, Yozan was transferred to a newly established subsidiary shrine, [[Matsugasaki Shrine]], and Uesugi Shrine once again exclusively enshrined Kenshin. In Taisho 8 (1919), a great fire destroyed the entire shrine precinct including the main hall. In Taisho 12 (1923), the current main hall and treasure hall "Keishoden" were reconstructed according to the design by Dr. [[Chuta Ito]] from Yonezawa City{{Cite web |url=https://yonezawa-kankou-navi.com/person/ito.html |title=Chuta Ito |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa City Tourism Campaign Promotion Council (Yonezawa City Tourism Section) |website=Yonezawa Tourism NAVI}}. ==Precincts== * main hall * Worship Hall * Keishoden (Treasure Hall) * Statue of Uesugi Kenshin located on the right side of the approach * Statue of Uesugi Yozan located along the approach * Statues of Uesugi Kagekatsu and Naoe Kanetsugu (Tenchijin statues) located along the approach * Kasuga Shrine * Fukutoku Inari Shrine * Memorial monument for the Akō incident, established by Tosuke Kimura File:UesugiShrine.JPG|Scene in the precincts (August 2009) File:Uesugi shrine 2.jpg|Approach ==Subsidiary Shrines== * [[Matsugasaki Shrine]] - Enshrines six deities including [[Uesugi Yozan]]. main hall | location = 1-4-13 Marunouchi, Yonezawa City, [[Yamagata Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|37|54|33.5|N|140|6|14.7|E|region:JP-06_scale:25000_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Uesugi Shrine}} | festival Deities = Lord [[Uesugi Kenshin]] | Shrine rank = Bekkaku Kanpeisha | established = Meiji 4 (1871) | festival = April 29 | deity = [[Uesugi Kenshin]] | Religious ceremony = | map = {{location map|Japan Yonezawa city#Japan Yamagata|label=Uesugi Shrine|position=center|width=200|float=center}} }} [[File:Uesugi kenshin.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Kenshin]] [[File:Uesugi-Yozan statue.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Yozan (located along the approach)]] '''Uesugi Shrine''' (うえすぎじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Yonezawa City]], [[Yamagata Prefecture]]. It is situated in [[Matsugasaki Park]] (the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]]) and enshrines [[Uesugi Kenshin]]. The former shrine rank was [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. It is one of the shrines that enshrine clan founders, which became popular from the late [[Edo period]] to the early [[Meiji period]]. Uesugi Shrine (上杉神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Yonezawa, Yamagata]].{{Cite web|last=Organization|first=Japan National Tourism|title=Uesugi-jinja Shrine {{!}} Travel Japan (Japan National Tourism Organization)|url=https://www.japan.travel/en/spot/434/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=Travel Japan|language=en-us}}{{Cite web|last=山形県観光物産協会|first=公益社団法人|title=Uesugi Jinja Shrine｜What to See & Do｜STAY YAMAGATA|url=https://yamagatakanko.com/en/attractions/detail_1390.html|access-date=2023-04-07|website=STAY YAMAGATA|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=TOKYO|first=COPYRIGHT © TOHOKU ×|title=Uesugi-Jinja Shrine {{!}} TOHOKU x TOKYO (JAPAN)|url=https://www.tohokuandtokyo.org/spot_131/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=www.tohokuandtokyo.org|language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo shrine]] and is dedicated to the memory of [[Uesugi Kenshin]], a famous military leader in Japanese history. The shrine was built in 1876 on the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]], and it enshrines the spirit of [[Uesugi Kenshin]]. Every year in February, a snow lantern festival is held at the shrine where lanterns are carved out of snow to honor the memory of Uesugi Kenshin. It is a popular event that attracts many visitors. ==History== When [[Uesugi Kenshin]] suddenly died in [[Tensho]] 6 (1578) at [[Kasugayama Castle]] in [[Echigo Province]], his remains were enshrined in a Buddhist manner at the Fushikian within the castle. However, when [[Uesugi Kagekatsu]] was transferred to [[Aizu Domain]] and later to [[Yonezawa]] in [[Keicho]] 6 (1601), Kenshin's shrine was also moved to Yonezawa. After that, eleven temples, with [[Ho-onji Temple]] as the chief temple, alternated in conducting the rites at the second bailey of Yonezawa Castle. However, in the Meiji period, due to the [[Shinbutsu Bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and the [[Haijo-rei]] (abolition of castles decree), Kenshin's remains were moved from the castle to the [[Uesugi family mausoleum]], and Ho-onji Temple was relocated in front of the mausoleum for its protection. Additionally, to enshrine Kenshin's spirit in a Shinto manner, a monk from Daijoji Temple, the second of the eleven temples, renounced the monkhood and became a Shinto priest. The priest adopted the surname Daijoji and the family continues to serve as the chief priest to this day. At the same time, the shrine also enshrined [[Uesugi Yozan]], a notable lord who revived the Yonezawa Domain, and it became "Uesugi Shrine" in Yamagata Prefecture. On May 21, Meiji 9 (1876), the shrine building was relocated to its current location, the former inner palace site of Yonezawa Castle. On April 26, Meiji 35 (1902), it was ranked as a [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. At this time, Yozan was transferred to a newly established subsidiary shrine, [[Matsugasaki Shrine]], and Uesugi Shrine once again exclusively enshrined Kenshin. In Taisho 8 (1919), a great fire destroyed the entire shrine precinct including the main hall. In Taisho 12 (1923), the current main hall and treasure hall "Keishoden" were reconstructed according to the design by Dr. [[Chuta Ito]] from Yonezawa City{{Cite web |url=https://yonezawa-kankou-navi.com/person/ito.html |title=Chuta Ito |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa City Tourism Campaign Promotion Council (Yonezawa City Tourism Section) |website=Yonezawa Tourism NAVI}}. ==Precincts== * main hall * Worship Hall * Keishoden (Treasure Hall) * Statue of Uesugi Kenshin located on the right side of the approach * Statue of Uesugi Yozan located along the approach * Statues of Uesugi Kagekatsu and Naoe Kanetsugu (Tenchijin statues) located along the approach * Kasuga Shrine * Fukutoku Inari Shrine * Memorial monument for the Akō incident, established by Tosuke Kimura File:UesugiShrine.JPG|Scene in the precincts (August 2009) File:Uesugi shrine 2.jpg|Approach ==Subsidiary Shrines== * [[Matsugasaki Shrine]] - Enshrines six deities including [[Uesugi Yozan]]. A statue of Yozan is located on the east side of the precincts (different in design from the statue on the approach to Uesugi Shrine). * [[Kasuga Shrine]] (in the precincts) - A shrine where Uesugi Yozan dedicated a pledge to study and train in martial arts, act justly, and award and punish fairly. * Fukutoku Inari Shrine (in the precincts) ==Major annual ceremony and Events== * [[January 1]] - Saitan festival and New Year's Prayers * [[January 15]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine fire rite * [[February 3]] - Setsubun festival * Second Saturday of February - Uesugi Snow Lantern festival Requiem Service * [[February 11]] - National Foundation Day Celebration * [[March 5]]–[[March 6]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine Old First Horse Day festival * Uesugi festival (April 28–May 3) ** [[April 28]] - Eve of the annual Grand festival ** [[April 29]] - annual Grand festival ** [[April 30]] - Matsugasaki Shrine festival ** [[April 30]] - Flower Offering festival ** [[May 1]] - Keishin Women's Association Spring Grand festival ** [[May 1]] - Carp Memorial Service ** [[May 2]] - Tea Offering festival ** [[May 3]] - Mikoshi Procession * Late May - Yozan Memorial festival (Rice Planting festival) * [[June 30]] - Great Purification ceremony * [[July 30]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine festival * [[September 25]] - Keizan Memorial Service * Last Saturday and Sunday of September - Matsugasaki Shrine Autumn Grand festival * Last Saturday and Sunday of September - Kasuga Shrine festival * Early October - Harvest festival * [[November 15]] - Shichi-Go-San Prayers * [[November 23]] - New Grain Thanksgiving festival * [[December 29]] - Old Talisman Burning ceremony * [[December 31]] - Great Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival ==Cultural Properties== [[File:Bishamonten (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|thumb|130px|right|Statue of Bishamonten (Late Heian period)]] [[File:Haramaki armour of Uesugi Kenshin.jpg|thumb|Iroiro-odoshi Haramaki with helmet and sleeve attachments, including black lacquer armor chest (allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin)]] '''[[Important Cultural Properties]]''' * Painted silk statue of Bishamonten * Purple damask golden mandala of the Two Realms * Painted silk statue of the Amida Triad (Koryo period, signed as Gen, second year of Zhida, 1309) (stolen in 1987) * Sword said to be made by Tomonari, with inscription on the front and the date of the third year of Kōan on the back * Sword with no inscription, with gold and silver inlay of Sanskrit characters and seven stars, with sheath decorated with the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac (allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin) * Sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Motoshige * Long sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Norikuni, with fittings * Long sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Katayama Ichimonji, with fittings * Long sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Katayama Ichimonji, with fittings * Spear inscribed "Made by Maeda" on December of the second year of Bunroku (10 items) * Iroiro-odoshi Haramaki with helmet and sleeve attachments, including black lacquer armor chest (allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin) * Garments allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin and Uesugi Kagekatsu (details provided later) * Light blue silk garment (allegedly used by Naoe Kanetsugu) * Collection of sutras including Wheel Mandala Box * Dark blue paper with gold characters of the Heart Sutra written by Emperor Go-Nara (stolen in 1987) * Sword signed "Sukemune," with leather-bound handle, used by Uesugi Kagekatsu (owned by Matsugasaki Shrine) * Ming court gifts to Uesugi Kagekatsu (1 hanging scroll) and Ming court garments (Sha Mao (expanded angle), rhinoceros horn belt, large red thread chestplate, green lining, shoes) These were split from the Important Cultural Properties "Garments allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin and Uesugi Kagekatsu" in 2018 (Notification No. 206 of the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, October 31, 2018) '''Other Cultural Properties''' * Gold small-laced light blue armor with accompanying helmet (used by Naoe Kanetsugu, known as the "Love" helmet)

{{-}} File:Amitabha Triad - Mahasthamaprapta (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Seishi Bodhisattva from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Amitabha Triad - Amitabha (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Amida Nyorai from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Amitabha Triad - a (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Kannon Bodhisattva from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Womb Realm Mandala (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|Purple Damask Golden Mudra Mandala of the Two Realms ==Carp Memorial== In Yonezawa, Uesugi Yozan encouraged the breeding and consumption of carp to provide a valuable protein source in the inland region. To promote the consumption of carp, "Carp Day" was established on [[May 1]], and since 1960, the Yonezawa Carp Merchants' Association has held the "Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival" to pray for business prosperity and memorialize the carp. During the festival, after the Shinto ceremony conducted by the chief priest of Uesugi Shrine, carp are released into the pond in the precincts. In the first year of the Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival, a monument to the carp memorial was erected in the precincts of Uesugi Shrine. The monument describes how, in 1810, a retainer of the Yonezawa Domain was sent to learn carp breeding methods in Edo's Honjo area and how, after his retirement, Uesugi Yozan established a nursery carp pond at Sankakukan and imported juvenile carp from Soma to sell as medicinal fish{{Cite web |url=https://www.yonezawa-np.jp/html/news/2023-S/20230502b.html |title=Carp Day (May 1), Carp Memorial festival at Uesugi Shrine |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa Nippo Digital |date=2023-05-02}}. ==Transportation Access== ===Rail=== * [[Ou Main Line]] (Yamagata Shinkansen) [[Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. * [[Yonesaka Line]] [[Minami-Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. ===Bus=== * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yamako Bus]] bound for [[Shirabu Onsen]], get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yonezawa City Community Bus]] City Loop Right Bus (blue bus) for 11 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From [[Sendai Station]], take the [[Express Bus]] Sendai-Yonezawa Line for 130 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. ===Road=== * Highway...From [[Tohoku Chuo Expressway]] [[Yonezawa Hachimanbara Interchange|Yonezawa Hachimanbara IC]], take [[Route 13]] towards Yamagata. It takes about 15 minutes by car from Route 13 Yonezawa Bypass. * National Route...From [[Kitakata]] use [[Route 121]], from [[Niigata City|Niigata]] use [[Route 113]]. * About 10 minutes by car from Yonezawa Station. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Related Books== * [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1112175/1/1 Compiled by Niroku Koshinjo, edited by Yonekichi Yamada, ''Seishi of Distinguished Shrine Bekkaku Kanpeisha,'' pp. 88-91, Niroku Koshinjo, 1935 (National Diet Library Digital Collection)] * Sukenari Azusa, Yoshihiko Umeda, editors and supervisors, ''Shinto Dictionary,'' Jinja Shinpōsha, [[1968]], p. 13 * Eiji Shirai, Masanori Toki, editors, ''Shrine Dictionary,'' [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], [[1979]], p. 52 ==See Also== {{Commonscat|Uesugi shrine}} * [[Chiura Obata]] {{Shinto temples}} {{Shinto-stub}} == References == {{Reflist}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages without meta categories]] [[Category:qq]] }} [[en:Uesugi Shrine]] [[ja:上杉神社]] [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]] {{citation needed|Uesugi Shrine}}

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Uesugi Shrine | image = [[File:Uesugi shrine 1.jpg|250px|]]
main hall | location = 1-4-13 Marunouchi, Yonezawa City, [[Yamagata Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|37|54|33.5|N|140|6|14.7|E|region:JP-06_scale:25000_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Uesugi Shrine}} | festival Deities = Lord [[Uesugi Kenshin]] | Shrine rank = Bekkaku Kanpeisha | established = Meiji 4 (1871) | festival = April 29 | deity = [[Uesugi Kenshin]] | Religious ceremony = | map = {{location map|Japan Yonezawa city#Japan Yamagata|label=Uesugi Shrine|position=center|width=200|float=center}} }} [[File:Uesugi kenshin.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Kenshin]] [[File:Uesugi-Yozan statue.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Yozan (located along the approach)]] '''Uesugi Shrine''' (うえすぎじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Yonezawa City]], [[Yamagata Prefecture]]. It is situated in [[Matsugasaki Park]] (the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]]) and enshrines [[Uesugi Kenshin]]. The former shrine rank was [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. It is one of the shrines that enshrine clan founders, which became popular from the late [[Edo period]] to the early [[Meiji period]]. Uesugi Shrine (上杉神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Yonezawa, Yamagata]].{{Cite web|last=Organization|first=Japan National Tourism|title=Uesugi-jinja Shrine {{!}} Travel Japan (Japan National Tourism Organization)|url=https://www.japan.travel/en/spot/434/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=Travel Japan|language=en-us}}{{Cite web|last=山形県観光物産協会|first=公益社団法人|title=Uesugi Jinja Shrine｜What to See & Do｜STAY YAMAGATA|url=https://yamagatakanko.com/en/attractions/detail_1390.html|access-date=2023-04-07|website=STAY YAMAGATA|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=TOKYO|first=COPYRIGHT © TOHOKU ×|title=Uesugi-Jinja Shrine {{!}} TOHOKU x TOKYO (JAPAN)|url=https://www.tohokuandtokyo.org/spot_131/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=www.tohokuandtokyo.org|language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo shrine]] and is dedicated to the memory of [[Uesugi Kenshin]], a famous military leader in Japanese history. The shrine was built in 1876 on the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]], and it enshrines the spirit of [[Uesugi Kenshin]]. Every year in February, a snow lantern festival is held at the shrine where lanterns are carved out of snow to honor the memory of Uesugi Kenshin. It is a popular event that attracts many visitors. ==History== When [[Uesugi Kenshin]] suddenly died in [[Tensho]] 6 (1578) at [[Kasugayama Castle]] in [[Echigo Province]], his remains were enshrined in a Buddhist manner at the Fushikian within the castle. However, when [[Uesugi Kagekatsu]] was transferred to [[Aizu Domain]] and later to [[Yonezawa]] in [[Keicho]] 6 (1601), Kenshin's shrine was also moved to Yonezawa. After that, eleven temples, with [[Ho-onji Temple]] as the chief temple, alternated in conducting the rites at the second bailey of Yonezawa Castle. However, in the Meiji period, due to the [[Shinbutsu Bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and the [[Haijo-rei]] (abolition of castles decree), Kenshin's remains were moved from the castle to the [[Uesugi family mausoleum]], and Ho-onji Temple was relocated in front of the mausoleum for its protection. Additionally, to enshrine Kenshin's spirit in a Shinto manner, a monk from Daijoji Temple, the second of the eleven temples, renounced the monkhood and became a Shinto priest. The priest adopted the surname Daijoji and the family continues to serve as the chief priest to this day. At the same time, the shrine also enshrined [[Uesugi Yozan]], a notable lord who revived the Yonezawa Domain, and it became "Uesugi Shrine" in Yamagata Prefecture. On May 21, Meiji 9 (1876), the shrine building was relocated to its current location, the former inner palace site of Yonezawa Castle. On April 26, Meiji 35 (1902), it was ranked as a [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. At this time, Yozan was transferred to a newly established subsidiary shrine, [[Matsugasaki Shrine]], and Uesugi Shrine once again exclusively enshrined Kenshin. In Taisho 8 (1919), a great fire destroyed the entire shrine precinct including the main hall. In Taisho 12 (1923), the current main hall and treasure hall "Keishoden" were reconstructed according to the design by Dr. [[Chuta Ito]] from Yonezawa City{{Cite web |url=https://yonezawa-kankou-navi.com/person/ito.html |title=Chuta Ito |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa City Tourism Campaign Promotion Council (Yonezawa City Tourism Section) |website=Yonezawa Tourism NAVI}}. ==Precincts== * main hall * Worship Hall * Keishoden (Treasure Hall) * Statue of Uesugi Kenshin located on the right side of the approach * Statue of Uesugi Yozan located along the approach * Statues of Uesugi Kagekatsu and Naoe Kanetsugu (Tenchijin statues) located along the approach * Kasuga Shrine * Fukutoku Inari Shrine * Memorial monument for the Akō incident, established by Tosuke Kimura File:UesugiShrine.JPG|Scene in the precincts (August 2009) File:Uesugi shrine 2.jpg|Approach ==Subsidiary Shrines== * [[Matsugasaki Shrine]] - Enshrines six deities including [[Uesugi Yozan]]. To promote the consumption of carp, "Carp Day" was established on [[May 1]], and since 1960, the Yonezawa Carp Merchants' Association has held the "Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival" to pray for business prosperity and memorialize the carp. During the festival, after the Shinto ceremony conducted by the chief priest of Uesugi Shrine, carp are released into the pond in the precincts. In the first year of the Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival, a monument to the carp memorial was erected in the precincts of Uesugi Shrine. The monument describes how, in 1810, a retainer of the Yonezawa Domain was sent to learn carp breeding methods in Edo's Honjo area and how, after his retirement, Uesugi Yozan established a nursery carp pond at Sankakukan and imported juvenile carp from Soma to sell as medicinal fish{{Cite web |url=https://www.yonezawa-np.jp/html/news/2023-S/20230502b.html |title=Carp Day (May 1), Carp Memorial festival at Uesugi Shrine |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa Nippo Digital |date=2023-05-02}}. ==Transportation Access== ===Rail=== * [[Ou Main Line]] (Yamagata Shinkansen) [[Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. * [[Yonesaka Line]] [[Minami-Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. ===Bus=== * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yamako Bus]] bound for [[Shirabu Onsen]], get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yonezawa City Community Bus]] City Loop Right Bus (blue bus) for 11 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From [[Sendai Station]], take the [[Express Bus]] Sendai-Yonezawa Line for 130 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. ===Road=== * Highway...From [[Tohoku Chuo Expressway]] [[Yonezawa Hachimanbara Interchange|Yonezawa Hachimanbara IC]], take [[Route 13]] towards Yamagata. It takes about 15 minutes by car from Route 13 Yonezawa Bypass. * National Route...From [[Kitakata]] use [[Route 121]], from [[Niigata City|Niigata]] use [[Route 113]]. * About 10 minutes by car from Yonezawa Station. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Related Books== * [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1112175/1/1 Compiled by Niroku Koshinjo, edited by Yonekichi Yamada, ''Seishi of Distinguished Shrine Bekkaku Kanpeisha,'' pp. 88-91, Niroku Koshinjo, 1935 (National Diet Library Digital Collection)] * Sukenari Azusa, Yoshihiko Umeda, editors and supervisors, ''Shinto Dictionary,'' Jinja Shinpōsha, [[1968]], p. 13 * Eiji Shirai, Masanori Toki, editors, ''Shrine Dictionary,'' [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], [[1979]], p. 52 ==See Also== {{Commonscat|Uesugi shrine}} * [[Chiura Obata]] {{Shinto temples}} {{Shinto-stub}} == References == {{Reflist}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages without meta categories]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Uesugi Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]] }} [[en:Uesugi Shrine]] [[ja:上杉神社]] [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]] {{citation needed|Uesugi Shrine}}

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Uesugi Shrine | image = [[File:Uesugi shrine 1.jpg|250px|]]
main hall | location = 1-4-13 Marunouchi, Yonezawa City, [[Yamagata Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|37|54|33.5|N|140|6|14.7|E|region:JP-06_scale:25000_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Uesugi Shrine}} | festival Deities = Lord [[Uesugi Kenshin]] | Shrine Rank = Bekkaku Kanpeisha | established = Meiji 4 (1871) | festival = April 29 | deity = [[Uesugi Kenshin]] | Religious ceremony = | map = {{location map|Japan Yonezawa city#Japan Yamagata|label=Uesugi Shrine|position=center|width=200|float=center}} }} [[File:Uesugi kenshin.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Kenshin]] [[File:Uesugi-Yozan statue.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Yozan (located along the approach)]] '''Uesugi Shrine''' (うえすぎじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Yonezawa City]], [[Yamagata Prefecture]]. It is situated in [[Matsugasaki Park]] (the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]]) and enshrines [[Uesugi Kenshin]]. The former shrine Rank was [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. It is one of the shrines that enshrine clan founders, which became popular from the late [[Edo period]] to the early [[Meiji period]]. Uesugi Shrine (上杉神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Yonezawa, Yamagata]].{{Cite web|last=Organization|first=Japan National Tourism|title=Uesugi-jinja Shrine {{!}} Travel Japan (Japan National Tourism Organization)|url=https://www.japan.travel/en/spot/434/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=Travel Japan|language=en-us}}{{Cite web|last=山形県観光物産協会|first=公益社団法人|title=Uesugi Jinja Shrine｜What to See & Do｜STAY YAMAGATA|url=https://yamagatakanko.com/en/attractions/detail_1390.html|access-date=2023-04-07|website=STAY YAMAGATA|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=TOKYO|first=COPYRIGHT © TOHOKU ×|title=Uesugi-Jinja Shrine {{!}} TOHOKU x TOKYO (JAPAN)|url=https://www.tohokuandtokyo.org/spot_131/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=www.tohokuandtokyo.org|language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo shrine]] and is dedicated to the memory of [[Uesugi Kenshin]], a famous military leader in Japanese history. The shrine was built in 1876 on the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]], and it enshrines the spirit of [[Uesugi Kenshin]]. Every year in February, a snow lantern festival is held at the shrine where lanterns are carved out of snow to honor the memory of Uesugi Kenshin. It is a popular event that attracts many visitors. ==History== When [[Uesugi Kenshin]] suddenly died in [[Tensho]] 6 (1578) at [[Kasugayama Castle]] in [[Echigo Province]], his remains were enshrined in a Buddhist manner at the Fushikian within the castle. However, when [[Uesugi Kagekatsu]] was transferred to [[Aizu Domain]] and later to [[Yonezawa]] in [[Keicho]] 6 (1601), Kenshin's shrine was also moved to Yonezawa. After that, eleven temples, with [[Ho-onji Temple]] as the chief temple, alternated in conducting the rites at the second bailey of Yonezawa Castle. However, in the Meiji period, due to the [[Shinbutsu Bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and the [[Haijo-rei]] (abolition of castles decree), Kenshin's remains were moved from the castle to the [[Uesugi family mausoleum]], and Ho-onji Temple was relocated in front of the mausoleum for its protection. Additionally, to enshrine Kenshin's spirit in a Shinto manner, a monk from Daijoji Temple, the second of the eleven temples, renounced the monkhood and became a Shinto priest. The priest adopted the surname Daijoji and the family continues to serve as the chief priest to this day. At the same time, the shrine also enshrined [[Uesugi Yozan]], a notable lord who revived the Yonezawa Domain, and it became "Uesugi Shrine" in Yamagata Prefecture. On May 21, Meiji 9 (1876), the shrine building was relocated to its current location, the former inner palace site of Yonezawa Castle. On April 26, Meiji 35 (1902), it was Ranked as a [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. At this time, Yozan was transferred to a newly established subsidiary shrine, [[Matsugasaki Shrine]], and Uesugi Shrine once again exclusively enshrined Kenshin. In Taisho 8 (1919), a great fire destroyed the entire shrine precinct including the main hall. In Taisho 12 (1923), the current main hall and treasure hall "Keishoden" were reconstructed according to the design by Dr. [[Chuta Ito]] from Yonezawa City{{Cite web |url=https://yonezawa-kankou-navi.com/person/ito.html |title=Chuta Ito |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa City Tourism Campaign Promotion Council (Yonezawa City Tourism Section) |website=Yonezawa Tourism NAVI}}. ==Precincts== * main hall * Worship Hall * Keishoden (Treasure Hall) * Statue of Uesugi Kenshin located on the right side of the approach * Statue of Uesugi Yozan located along the approach * Statues of Uesugi Kagekatsu and Naoe Kanetsugu (Tenchijin statues) located along the approach * Kasuga Shrine * Fukutoku Inari Shrine * Memorial monument for the Akō incident, established by Tosuke Kimura File:UesugiShrine.JPG|Scene in the precincts (August 2009) File:Uesugi shrine 2.jpg|Approach ==Subsidiary Shrines== * [[Matsugasaki Shrine]] - Enshrines six deities including [[Uesugi Yozan]]. A statue of Yozan is located on the east side of the precincts (different in design from the statue on the approach to Uesugi Shrine). * [[Kasuga Shrine]] (in the precincts) - A shrine where Uesugi Yozan dedicated a pledge to study and train in martial arts, act justly, and award and punish fairly. * Fukutoku Inari Shrine (in the precincts) ==Major annual ceremony and Events== * [[January 1]] - Saitan festival and New Year's Prayers * [[January 15]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine fire rite * [[February 3]] - Setsubun festival * Second Saturday of February - Uesugi Snow Lantern festival Requiem Service * [[February 11]] - National Foundation Day Celebration * [[March 5]]–[[March 6]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine Old First Horse Day festival * Uesugi festival (April 28–May 3) ** [[April 28]] - Eve of the annual Grand festival ** [[April 29]] - annual Grand festival ** [[April 30]] - Matsugasaki Shrine festival ** [[April 30]] - Flower Offering festival ** [[May 1]] - Keishin Women's Association Spring Grand festival ** [[May 1]] - Carp Memorial Service ** [[May 2]] - Tea Offering festival ** [[May 3]] - Mikoshi Procession * Late May - Yozan Memorial festival (Rice Planting festival) * [[June 30]] - Great Purification ceremony * [[July 30]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine festival * [[September 25]] - Keizan Memorial Service * Last Saturday and Sunday of September - Matsugasaki Shrine Autumn Grand festival * Last Saturday and Sunday of September - Kasuga Shrine festival * Early October - Harvest festival * [[November 15]] - Shichi-Go-San Prayers * [[November 23]] - New Grain Thanksgiving festival * [[December 29]] - Old Talisman Burning ceremony * [[December 31]] - Great Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival ==Cultural Properties== [[File:Bishamonten (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|thumb|130px|right|Statue of Bishamonten (Late Heian period)]] [[File:Haramaki armour of Uesugi Kenshin.jpg|thumb|Iroiro-odoshi Haramaki with helmet and sleeve attachments, including black lacquer armor chest (allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin)]] '''[[Important Cultural Properties]]''' * Painted silk statue of Bishamonten * Purple damask golden mandala of the Two Realms * Painted silk statue of the Amida Triad (Koryo period, signed as Gen, second year of Zhida, 1309) (stolen in 1987) * Sword said to be made by Tomonari, with inscription on the front and the date of the third year of Kōan on the back * Sword with no inscription, with gold and silver inlay of Sanskrit characters and seven stars, with sheath decorated with the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac (allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin) * Sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Motoshige * Long sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Norikuni, with fittings * Long sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Katayama Ichimonji, with fittings * Long sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Katayama Ichimonji, with fittings * Spear inscribed "Made by Maeda" on December of the second year of Bunroku (10 items) * Iroiro-odoshi Haramaki with helmet and sleeve attachments, including black lacquer armor chest (allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin) * Garments allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin and Uesugi Kagekatsu (details provided later) * Light blue silk garment (allegedly used by Naoe Kanetsugu) * Collection of sutras including Wheel Mandala Box * Dark blue paper with gold characters of the Heart Sutra written by Emperor Go-Nara (stolen in 1987) * Sword signed "Sukemune," with leather-bound handle, used by Uesugi Kagekatsu (owned by Matsugasaki Shrine) * Ming court gifts to Uesugi Kagekatsu (1 hanging scroll) and Ming court garments (Sha Mao (expanded angle), rhinoceros horn belt, large red thread chestplate, green lining, shoes) These were split from the Important Cultural Properties "Garments allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin and Uesugi Kagekatsu" in 2018 (Notification No. 206 of the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, October 31, 2018) '''Other Cultural Properties''' * Gold small-laced light blue armor with accompanying helmet (used by Naoe Kanetsugu, known as the "Love" helmet)

{{神社 | 名称=上杉神社 | 画像=[[ファイル:Uesugi shrine 1.jpg|250px|]]
拝殿 | 所在地=[[山形県]][[米沢市]]丸の内1丁目4-13 | 位置={{Coord|37|54|33.5|N|140|6|14.7|E|region:JP-06_scale:25000_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=上杉神社}} | 祭神=[[上杉謙信]]公 | 社格=別格官幣社 | 創建=[[明治]]4年（[[1871年]]） | 例祭=[[4月29日]] | 神事= | 地図={{Location map|Japan Yonezawa city#Japan Yamagata|label=上杉神社|position=center|width=200|float=center}} }} [[ファイル:Uesugi kenshin.jpg|thumbnail|150px|上杉謙信像]] [[ファイル:Uesugi-Yozan statue.jpg|thumbnail|150px|上杉鷹山像（参道に立つもの）]] '''上杉神社'''（うえすぎじんじゃ）は、[[山形県]][[米沢市]]にある[[神社]]。[[松岬公園|松が岬公園]]（[[米沢城]]址）に位置し、[[上杉謙信]]を祀る。旧社格は[[別格官幣社]]。[[江戸時代]]後期から[[明治時代]]初期に流行した[[藩祖]]を祀った神社のひとつ。 ==歴史== [[上杉謙信]]が[[天正]]6年（[[1578年]]）、[[越後国|越後]][[春日山城]]で急死した際、遺骸は城内の不識庵に仏式にて祭られたが、次代の[[上杉景勝]]が[[会津藩|会津]]を経て[[慶長]]6年（[[1601年]]）に[[米沢藩|米沢]]へ移封されたのに合わせ、謙信の祠堂も米沢に遷された。 以後、米沢城二の丸の[[法音寺 (米沢市)|法音寺]]を首席とする十一ヶ寺が交代で祭祀を執り行ってきたが、[[明治]]に入ると[[神仏分離令]]、[[廃城令]]などにより、謙信の遺骸が城内から[[上杉家廟所]]に移され、その守護のために法音寺も廟所前に移転した。更に、城内に留まっている謙信の霊魂を神式で祀るため、十一ヶ寺次席の大乗寺の僧侶が還俗して神官となった。この時、姓を大乗寺とし、現在も同家で[[宮司]]職を務めている。 併せて米沢藩中興の名君である[[上杉治憲|上杉鷹山]]を合祀し、山形県社「上杉神社」とした。明治9年（[[1876年]]）[[5月21日]]、現在の旧米沢城奥御殿跡に社殿が遷座された。 明治35年（[[1902年]]）[[4月26日]]には別格官幣社に列せられる。この時鷹山は新たに設けた摂社「[[松岬神社]]」に遷され、上杉神社は再び謙信のみを祀ることとなった。 [[大正]]8年（[[1919年]]）の大火で境内は本殿以下全焼し、大正12年（1923年）、[[米沢市]]出身の[[伊東忠太]]博士の設計により、現在の本殿と宝物殿「稽照殿（けいしょうでん）」が再建された{{Cite web |url=https://yonezawa-kankou-navi.com/person/ito.html |title=伊東忠太 |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=米沢市観光キャンペーン推進協議会（米沢市観光課内） |website=米沢観光NAVI}}。 ==境内== *本殿 *拝殿 *稽照殿（宝物殿） *上杉謙信公像　参道を右手に入ったところに立つ。 *上杉鷹山公像　参道沿いに立つ。 *上杉景勝公と直江兼続公像（天地人像）　参道沿いに立つ。 *春日神社 *福徳稲荷神社 *[[赤穂事件]]殉難追悼碑 - [[木村東介]]建立 File:UesugiShrine.JPG|境内の様子（2009年8月） File:Uesugi shrine 2.jpg|参道 ==摂社== *[[松岬神社]]　[[上杉治憲|上杉鷹山]]ほか計6柱を祀る。境内東側に鷹山の像がある（意匠は上杉神社参道に立つ像と異なる）。 *[[春日神社]]（境内）　上杉鷹山公が学問・武芸に励むことや、行動や賞罰に不正の無いこと等を誓った誓詞を奉納した神社 *福徳稲荷神社（境内） ==主な神事・年中行事== *[[1月1日]] - 歳旦祭並びに新春祈祷 *[[1月15日|１月15日]] - 末社福徳稲荷神社　さいと焼き *[[2月3日]] - 節分祭 *2月第2土曜日 - 上杉雪灯篭まつり　鎮魂祭 *[[2月11日]] - 建国記念の日奉祝祭 *[[3月5日]]～[[3月6日]] - 末社福徳稲荷神社旧初午祭 *上杉まつり（4月28日～5月3日） **[[4月28日]] - 例大祭前夜祭 **[[4月29日]] - 例大祭 **[[4月30日]] - 摂社松岬神社例祭 **[[4月30日]] - 献華祭 **[[5月1日]] - 敬神婦人会春季大祭 **[[5月1日]] - 鯉供養 **[[5月2日]] - 献茶祭 **[[5月3日]] - 神輿渡御 *５月下旬 - 鷹山公藉田祭（お田植祭） *[[6月30日|６月30日]] - 大祓式 *[[7月30日|７月30日]] - 末社福徳稲荷神社例祭 *[[9月25日]] - 曦山公碑前祭 *９月最終土日 - 摂社松岬神社秋季大祭 *９月最終土日 - 春日神社例祭 *10月上旬 - 抜穂祭 *[[11月15日]] - 七五三祈祷 *[[11月23日]] - 新穀感謝祭 *[[12月29日]] - 古札焼納祭 *[[12月31日]] - 大祓式・除夜祭 ==文化財== [[File:Bishamonten (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|thumb|130px|right|毘沙門天像（平安時代後期）]] [[File:Haramaki armour of Uesugi Kenshin.jpg|thumb|色々威腹巻 兜・壺袖付 附黒漆鎧櫃（伝 上杉謙信所用）]] '''[[重要文化財]]''' *絹本著色毘沙門天像 *紫綾金泥両界曼荼羅図 *絹本著色阿弥陀三尊像 高麗時代 元の至大二年（1309年）在銘（[[1987年]]盗難） *太刀 伝 倫光作　表に備前国（以下不明）裏に興国三年云々の銘あり *剣 無銘 梵字及び七星の金銀象嵌あり 十二支蒔絵鞘付（伝 上杉謙信 所用） *太刀 無銘　伝 元重 *長巻 無銘　伝 則包 拵（こしらえ）付 *長巻 無銘　伝 片山一文字 拵付 *長巻 無銘　伝 片山一文字 拵付 *鑓（やり） 銘城州埋忠作 文禄二年十二月日 10本 *色々威腹巻 兜・壺袖付 附黒漆鎧櫃（伝 上杉謙信所用） *服飾類（伝 上杉謙信 上杉景勝所用）（明細は後出） *浅葱地花葉文緞子胴服（伝 直江兼続所用） *綜芸種智院式　附:輪羯磨蒔絵箱 *紺紙金字後奈良天皇宸翰般若心経（1987年盗難） *太刀 銘助宗 拵革柄革包太刀 上杉景勝所用（摂社松岬神社所有） *明国箚付（みんこくさっぷ） 上杉景勝宛（1幅）、明冠服類（みんかんぷくるい）（文禄五年上杉景勝受贈）（紗帽（展角付）、犀角帯、大紅刻糸胸背斗牛円領、緑貼裏、靴）重要文化財「服飾類（伝 上杉謙信 上杉景勝所用）」の一部として指定されていたものから2018年に分割指定（平成30年10月31日文部科学省告示第206号） '''その他の文化財''' *金小札浅葱糸威二枚胴具足 付属兜（[[直江兼続]]所用、通称「愛」の兜）

{{-}} File:Amitabha Triad - Mahasthamaprapta (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|阿弥陀三尊像（高麗時代）のうち勢至菩薩 File:Amitabha Triad - Amitabha (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|阿弥陀三尊像（高麗時代）のうち阿弥陀如来 File:Amitabha Triad - a (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|阿弥陀三尊像（高麗時代）のうち観音菩薩 File:Womb Realm Mandala (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|紫綾金泥両界曼荼羅図 == 鯉供養 == 上杉鷹山が海から遠い米沢で、貴重なタンパク源を得るために、藩士に鯉を飼わせ、鯉を食べることを奨励したことから、米沢では鯉の食文化が根付いている。鯉の消費拡大を図るために制定された[[5月1日]]の「鯉の日」に、米沢鯉商組合では[[1960年]]（昭和35年）から、鯉の供養と商売繁盛を祈念して「米沢鯉供養祭」を開催している。供養祭では、上杉神社宮司による神事のあとに、鯉が境内の池に放生（ほうじょう）される。 米沢鯉供養祭が初開催された昭和35年、上杉神社境内には鯉供養之碑が建立された。そこには文化7年（1810年）に、米沢藩支藩の家臣を江戸本所に派遣して鯉の飼育方法を学ばせたことや、その後、上杉鷹山が隠居後に住んだ餐霞館に苗鯉池を設け、鯉を薬用魚として販売していくため、相馬から稚魚を取り寄せたことなどが書かれている{{Cite web |url=https://www.yonezawa-np.jp/html/news/2023-S/20230502b.html |title=鯉の日（５／１）、上杉神社境内で鯉供養祭 |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=米沢日報デジタル |date=2023-05-02}}。 ==交通アクセス== ===鉄道=== *[[奥羽本線]]（[[山形新幹線]]）[[米沢駅]]から徒歩で約20分。 *[[米坂線]][[南米沢駅]]から徒歩で約20分。 ===バス=== *米沢駅から[[山交バス (山形県)|山交バス]][[白布温泉]]行きで8分。「上杉神社前」で下車、徒歩3分。 *米沢駅から[[米沢市市民バス|市民バス]]市街地循環右回りバス（青色のバス）で11分。「上杉神社前」で下車、徒歩3分。 *[[仙台駅]]から[[高速バス]]・[[仙台 - 米沢線]]で130分。「上杉神社前」で下車、徒歩3分。 ===道路=== *高速道路…[[東北中央自動車道]][[米沢八幡原インターチェンジ|米沢八幡原IC]]から[[国道13号]]を山形方面へ。13号[[米沢バイパス]]から車で約15分。 *一般国道…[[喜多方市|喜多方]]方面からは[[国道121号]]、[[新潟市|新潟]]方面からは[[国道113号]]をそれぞれ利用。 *米沢駅から車で約10分。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == 関連図書 == * [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1112175/1/1 二六興信所編纂　山田米吉編『勤王事蹟別格官幣社精史』88〜91頁　二六興信所　1935年（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）] *安津素彦・梅田義彦編集兼監修者『神道辞典』神社新報社、[[1968年]]、13頁 *白井永二・土岐昌訓編集『神社辞典』[[東京堂出版]]、[[1979年]]、52頁 == 関連項目 == {{Commonscat|Uesugi shrine}} *[[小圃千浦]] {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{Shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:うえすきしんしや}} [[Category:山形県の神社]] [[Category:米沢市の歴史]] [[Category:米沢藩]] [[Category:山形県の重要文化財]] [[Category:別格官幣社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:山形県の登録有形文化財]] [[Category:長尾上杉家|宗教うえすきしんしや]] [[Category:米沢市の建築物]] [[Category:上杉景勝]] [[Category:上杉謙信]] [[Category:上杉鷹山]] [[Category:伊東忠太]]

拝殿 | 所在地=[[山形県]][[米沢市]]丸の内1丁目4-13 | 位置={{Coord|37|54|33.5|N|140|6|14.7|E|region:JP-06_scale:25000_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=上杉神社}} | 祭神=[[上杉謙信]]公 | 社格=別格官幣社 | 創建=[[明治]]4年（[[1871年]]） | 例祭=[[4月29日]] | 神事= | 地図={{Location map|Japan Yonezawa city#Japan Yamagata|label=上杉神社|position=center|width=200|float=center}} }} [[ファイル:Uesugi kenshin.jpg|thumbnail|150px|上杉謙信像]] [[ファイル:Uesugi-Yozan statue.jpg|thumbnail|150px|上杉鷹山像（参道に立つもの）]] '''上杉神社'''（うえすぎじんじゃ）は、[[山形県]][[米沢市]]にある[[神社]]。[[松岬公園|松が岬公園]]（[[米沢城]]址）に位置し、[[上杉謙信]]を祀る。旧社格は[[別格官幣社]]。[[江戸時代]]後期から[[明治時代]]初期に流行した[[藩祖]]を祀った神社のひとつ。 ==歴史== [[上杉謙信]]が[[天正]]6年（[[1578年]]）、[[越後国|越後]][[春日山城]]で急死した際、遺骸は城内の不識庵に仏式にて祭られたが、次代の[[上杉景勝]]が[[会津藩|会津]]を経て[[慶長]]6年（[[1601年]]）に[[米沢藩|米沢]]へ移封されたのに合わせ、謙信の祠堂も米沢に遷された。 以後、米沢城二の丸の[[法音寺 (米沢市)|法音寺]]を首席とする十一ヶ寺が交代で祭祀を執り行ってきたが、[[明治]]に入ると[[神仏分離令]]、[[廃城令]]などにより、謙信の遺骸が城内から[[上杉家廟所]]に移され、その守護のために法音寺も廟所前に移転した。更に、城内に留まっている謙信の霊魂を神式で祀るため、十一ヶ寺次席の大乗寺の僧侶が還俗して神官となった。この時、姓を大乗寺とし、現在も同家で[[宮司]]職を務めている。 併せて米沢藩中興の名君である[[上杉治憲|上杉鷹山]]を合祀し、山形県社「上杉神社」とした。明治9年（[[1876年]]）[[5月21日]]、現在の旧米沢城奥御殿跡に社殿が遷座された。 明治35年（[[1902年]]）[[4月26日]]には別格官幣社に列せられる。この時鷹山は新たに設けた摂社「[[松岬神社]]」に遷され、上杉神社は再び謙信のみを祀ることとなった。 [[大正]]8年（[[1919年]]）の大火で境内は本殿以下全焼し、大正12年（1923年）、[[米沢市]]出身の[[伊東忠太]]博士の設計により、現在の本殿と宝物殿「稽照殿（けいしょうでん）」が再建された{{Cite web |url=https://yonezawa-kankou-navi.com/person/ito.html |title=伊東忠太 |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=米沢市観光キャンペーン推進協議会（米沢市観光課内） |website=米沢観光NAVI}}。 ==境内== *本殿 *拝殿 *稽照殿（宝物殿） *上杉謙信公像　参道を右手に入ったところに立つ。 *上杉鷹山公像　参道沿いに立つ。 *上杉景勝公と直江兼続公像（天地人像）　参道沿いに立つ。 *春日神社 *福徳稲荷神社 *[[赤穂事件]]殉難追悼碑 - [[木村東介]]建立 File:UesugiShrine.JPG|境内の様子（2009年8月） File:Uesugi shrine 2.jpg|参道 ==摂社== *[[松岬神社]]　[[上杉治憲|上杉鷹山]]ほか計6柱を祀る。境内東側に鷹山の像がある（意匠は上杉神社参道に立つ像と異なる）。 *[[春日神社]]（境内）　上杉鷹山公が学問・武芸に励むことや、行動や賞罰に不正の無いこと等を誓った誓詞を奉納した神社 *福徳稲荷神社（境内） ==主な神事・年中行事== *[[1月1日]] - 歳旦祭並びに新春祈祷 *[[1月15日|１月15日]] - 末社福徳稲荷神社　さいと焼き *[[2月3日]] - 節分祭 *2月第2土曜日 - 上杉雪灯篭まつり　鎮魂祭 *[[2月11日]] - 建国記念の日奉祝祭 *[[3月5日]]～[[3月6日]] - 末社福徳稲荷神社旧初午祭 *上杉まつり（4月28日～5月3日） **[[4月28日]] - 例大祭前夜祭 **[[4月29日]] - 例大祭 **[[4月30日]] - 摂社松岬神社例祭 **[[4月30日]] - 献華祭 **[[5月1日]] - 敬神婦人会春季大祭 **[[5月1日]] - 鯉供養 **[[5月2日]] - 献茶祭 **[[5月3日]] - 神輿渡御 *５月下旬 - 鷹山公藉田祭（お田植祭） *[[6月30日|６月30日]] - 大祓式 *[[7月30日|７月30日]] - 末社福徳稲荷神社例祭 *[[9月25日]] - 曦山公碑前祭 *９月最終土日 - 摂社松岬神社秋季大祭 *９月最終土日 - 春日神社例祭 *10月上旬 - 抜穂祭 *[[11月15日]] - 七五三祈祷 *[[11月23日]] - 新穀感謝祭 *[[12月29日]] - 古札焼納祭 *[[12月31日]] - 大祓式・除夜祭 ==文化財== [[File:Bishamonten (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|thumb|130px|right|毘沙門天像（平安時代後期）]] [[File:Haramaki armour of Uesugi Kenshin.jpg|thumb|色々威腹巻 兜・壺袖付 附黒漆鎧櫃（伝 上杉謙信所用）]] '''[[重要文化財]]''' *絹本著色毘沙門天像 *紫綾金泥両界曼荼羅図 *絹本著色阿弥陀三尊像 高麗時代 元の至大二年（1309年）在銘（[[1987年]]盗難） *太刀 伝 倫光作　表に備前国（以下不明）裏に興国三年云々の銘あり *剣 無銘 梵字及び七星の金銀象嵌あり 十二支蒔絵鞘付（伝 上杉謙信 所用） *太刀 無銘　伝 元重 *長巻 無銘　伝 則包 拵（こしらえ）付 *長巻 無銘　伝 片山一文字 拵付 *長巻 無銘　伝 片山一文字 拵付 *鑓（やり） 銘城州埋忠作 文禄二年十二月日 10本 *色々威腹巻 兜・壺袖付 附黒漆鎧櫃（伝 上杉謙信所用） *服飾類（伝 上杉謙信 上杉景勝所用）（明細は後出） *浅葱地花葉文緞子胴服（伝 直江兼続所用） *綜芸種智院式　附:輪羯磨蒔絵箱 *紺紙金字後奈良天皇宸翰般若心経（1987年盗難） *太刀 銘助宗 拵革柄革包太刀 上杉景勝所用（摂社松岬神社所有） *明国箚付（みんこくさっぷ） 上杉景勝宛（1幅）、明冠服類（みんかんぷくるい）（文禄五年上杉景勝受贈）（紗帽（展角付）、犀角帯、大紅刻糸胸背斗牛円領、緑貼裏、靴）重要文化財「服飾類（伝 上杉謙信 上杉景勝所用）」の一部として指定されていたものから2018年に分割指定（平成30年10月31日文部科学省告示第206号） '''その他の文化財''' *金小札浅葱糸威二枚胴具足 付属兜（[[直江兼続]]所用、通称「愛」の兜）

{{-}} File:Amitabha Triad - Mahasthamaprapta (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|阿弥陀三尊像（高麗時代）のうち勢至菩薩 File:Amitabha Triad - Amitabha (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|阿弥陀三尊像（高麗時代）のうち阿弥陀如来 File:Amitabha Triad - a (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|阿弥陀三尊像（高麗時代）のうち観音菩薩 File:Womb Realm Mandala (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|紫綾金泥両界曼荼羅図 == 鯉供養 == 上杉鷹山が海から遠い米沢で、貴重なタンパク源を得るために、藩士に鯉を飼わせ、鯉を食べることを奨励したことから、米沢では鯉の食文化が根付いている。鯉の消費拡大を図るために制定された[[5月1日]]の「鯉の日」に、米沢鯉商組合では[[1960年]]（昭和35年）から、鯉の供養と商売繁盛を祈念して「米沢鯉供養祭」を開催している。供養祭では、上杉神社宮司による神事のあとに、鯉が境内の池に放生（ほうじょう）される。 米沢鯉供養祭が初開催された昭和35年、上杉神社境内には鯉供養之碑が建立された。そこには文化7年（1810年）に、米沢藩支藩の家臣を江戸本所に派遣して鯉の飼育方法を学ばせたことや、その後、上杉鷹山が隠居後に住んだ餐霞館に苗鯉池を設け、鯉を薬用魚として販売していくため、相馬から稚魚を取り寄せたことなどが書かれている{{Cite web |url=https://www.yonezawa-np.jp/html/news/2023-S/20230502b.html |title=鯉の日（５／１）、上杉神社境内で鯉供養祭 |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=米沢日報デジタル |date=2023-05-02}}。 ==交通アクセス== ===鉄道=== *[[奥羽本線]]（[[山形新幹線]]）[[米沢駅]]から徒歩で約20分。 *[[米坂線]][[南米沢駅]]から徒歩で約20分。 ===バス=== *米沢駅から[[山交バス (山形県)|山交バス]][[白布温泉]]行きで8分。「上杉神社前」で下車、徒歩3分。 *米沢駅から[[米沢市市民バス|市民バス]]市街地循環右回りバス（青色のバス）で11分。「上杉神社前」で下車、徒歩3分。 *[[仙台駅]]から[[高速バス]]・[[仙台 - 米沢線]]で130分。「上杉神社前」で下車、徒歩3分。 ===道路=== *高速道路…[[東北中央自動車道]][[米沢八幡原インターチェンジ|米沢八幡原IC]]から[[国道13号]]を山形方面へ。13号[[米沢バイパス]]から車で約15分。 *一般国道…[[喜多方市|喜多方]]方面からは[[国道121号]]、[[新潟市|新潟]]方面からは[[国道113号]]をそれぞれ利用。 *米沢駅から車で約10分。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == 関連図書 == * [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1112175/1/1 二六興信所編纂　山田米吉編『勤王事蹟別格官幣社精史』88〜91頁　二六興信所　1935年（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）] *安津素彦・梅田義彦編集兼監修者『神道辞典』神社新報社、[[1968年]]、13頁 *白井永二・土岐昌訓編集『神社辞典』[[東京堂出版]]、[[1979年]]、52頁 == 関連項目 == {{Commonscat|Uesugi shrine}} *[[小圃千浦]] {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{Shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:うえすきしんしや}} [[Category:山形県の神社]] [[Category:米沢市の歴史]] [[Category:米沢藩]] [[Category:山形県の重要文化財]] [[Category:別格官幣社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:山形県の登録有形文化財]] [[Category:長尾上杉家|宗教うえすきしんしや]] [[Category:米沢市の建築物]] [[Category:上杉景勝]] [[Category:上杉謙信]] [[Category:上杉鷹山]] [[Category:伊東忠太]]

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Uesugi Shrine | image = [[File:Uesugi shrine 1.jpg|250px|]]
main hall | location = 1-4-13 Marunouchi, Yonezawa City, [[Yamagata Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|37|54|33.5|N|140|6|14.7|E|region:JP-06_scale:25000_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Uesugi Shrine}} | festival Deities = Lord [[Uesugi Kenshin]] | Shrine Rank = Bekkaku Kanpeisha | established = Meiji 4 (1871) | festival = April 29 | deity = [[Uesugi Kenshin]] | Religious ceremony = | map = {{location map|Japan Yonezawa city#Japan Yamagata|label=Uesugi Shrine|position=center|width=200|float=center}} }} [[File:Uesugi kenshin.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Kenshin]] [[File:Uesugi-Yozan statue.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Yozan (located along the approach)]] '''Uesugi Shrine''' (うえすぎじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Yonezawa City]], [[Yamagata Prefecture]]. It is situated in [[Matsugasaki Park]] (the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]]) and enshrines [[Uesugi Kenshin]]. The former shrine Rank was [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. It is one of the shrines that enshrine clan founders, which became popular from the late [[Edo period]] to the early [[Meiji period]]. Uesugi Shrine (上杉神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Yonezawa, Yamagata]].{{Cite web|last=Organization|first=Japan National Tourism|title=Uesugi-jinja Shrine {{!}} Travel Japan (Japan National Tourism Organization)|url=https://www.japan.travel/en/spot/434/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=Travel Japan|language=en-us}}{{Cite web|last=山形県観光物産協会|first=公益社団法人|title=Uesugi Jinja Shrine｜What to See & Do｜STAY YAMAGATA|url=https://yamagatakanko.com/en/attractions/detail_1390.html|access-date=2023-04-07|website=STAY YAMAGATA|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=TOKYO|first=COPYRIGHT © TOHOKU ×|title=Uesugi-Jinja Shrine {{!}} TOHOKU x TOKYO (JAPAN)|url=https://www.tohokuandtokyo.org/spot_131/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=www.tohokuandtokyo.org|language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo shrine]] and is dedicated to the memory of [[Uesugi Kenshin]], a famous military leader in Japanese history. The shrine was built in 1876 on the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]], and it enshrines the spirit of [[Uesugi Kenshin]]. Every year in February, a snow lantern festival is held at the shrine where lanterns are carved out of snow to honor the memory of Uesugi Kenshin. It is a popular event that attracts many visitors. ==History== When [[Uesugi Kenshin]] suddenly died in [[Tensho]] 6 (1578) at [[Kasugayama Castle]] in [[Echigo Province]], his remains were enshrined in a Buddhist manner at the Fushikian within the castle. However, when [[Uesugi Kagekatsu]] was transferred to [[Aizu Domain]] and later to [[Yonezawa]] in [[Keicho]] 6 (1601), Kenshin's shrine was also moved to Yonezawa. After that, eleven temples, with [[Ho-onji Temple]] as the chief temple, alternated in conducting the rites at the second bailey of Yonezawa Castle. However, in the Meiji period, due to the [[Shinbutsu Bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and the [[Haijo-rei]] (abolition of castles decree), Kenshin's remains were moved from the castle to the [[Uesugi family mausoleum]], and Ho-onji Temple was relocated in front of the mausoleum for its protection. Additionally, to enshrine Kenshin's spirit in a Shinto manner, a monk from Daijoji Temple, the second of the eleven temples, renounced the monkhood and became a Shinto priest. The priest adopted the surname Daijoji and the family continues to serve as the chief priest to this day. At the same time, the shrine also enshrined [[Uesugi Yozan]], a notable lord who revived the Yonezawa Domain, and it became "Uesugi Shrine" in Yamagata Prefecture. On May 21, Meiji 9 (1876), the shrine building was relocated to its current location, the former inner palace site of Yonezawa Castle. {{-}} File:Amitabha Triad - Mahasthamaprapta (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Seishi Bodhisattva from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Amitabha Triad - Amitabha (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Amida Nyorai from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Amitabha Triad - a (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Kannon Bodhisattva from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Womb Realm Mandala (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|Purple Damask Golden Mudra Mandala of the Two Realms ==Carp Memorial== In Yonezawa, Uesugi Yozan encouraged the breeding and consumption of carp to provide a valuable protein source in the inland region. To promote the consumption of carp, "Carp Day" was established on [[May 1]], and since 1960, the Yonezawa Carp Merchants' Association has held the "Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival" to pray for business prosperity and memorialize the carp. During the festival, after the Shinto ceremony conducted by the chief priest of Uesugi Shrine, carp are released into the pond in the precincts. In the first year of the Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival, a monument to the carp memorial was erected in the precincts of Uesugi Shrine. The monument describes how, in 1810, a retainer of the Yonezawa Domain was sent to learn carp breeding methods in Edo's Honjo area and how, after his retirement, Uesugi Yozan established a nursery carp pond at Sankakukan and imported juvenile carp from Soma to sell as medicinal fish{{Cite web |url=https://www.yonezawa-np.jp/html/news/2023-S/20230502b.html |title=Carp Day (May 1), Carp Memorial festival at Uesugi Shrine |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa Nippo Digital |date=2023-05-02}}. ==Transportation Access== ===Rail=== * [[Ou Main Line]] (Yamagata Shinkansen) [[Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. * [[Yonesaka Line]] [[Minami-Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. ===Bus=== * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yamako Bus]] bound for [[Shirabu Onsen]], get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yonezawa City Community Bus]] City Loop Right Bus (blue bus) for 11 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From [[Sendai Station]], take the [[Express Bus]] Sendai-Yonezawa Line for 130 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. ===Road=== * Highway...From [[Tohoku Chuo Expressway]] [[Yonezawa Hachimanbara Interchange|Yonezawa Hachimanbara IC]], take [[Route 13]] towards Yamagata. It takes about 15 minutes by car from Route 13 Yonezawa Bypass. * National Route...From [[Kitakata]] use [[Route 121]], from [[Niigata City|Niigata]] use [[Route 113]]. * About 10 minutes by car from Yonezawa Station. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Related Books== * [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1112175/1/1 Compiled by Niroku Koshinjo, edited by Yonekichi Yamada, ''Seishi of Distinguished Shrine Bekkaku Kanpeisha,'' pp. 88-91, Niroku Koshinjo, 1935 (National Diet Library Digital Collection)] * Sukenari Azusa, Yoshihiko Umeda, editors and supervisors, ''Shinto Dictionary,'' Jinja Shinpōsha, [[1968]], p. 13 * Eiji Shirai, Masanori Toki, editors, ''Shrine Dictionary,'' [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], [[1979]], p. 52 ==See Also== {{Commonscat|Uesugi shrine}} * [[Chiura Obata]] {{Shinto temples}} {{Shinto-stub}} == References == {{Reflist}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages without meta categories]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Uesugi Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]] }} [[en:Uesugi Shrine]] [[ja:上杉神社]] [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]] {{citation needed|Uesugi Shrine}} {{translated page|ja|上杉神社|version=98634141|comment=Imported full ja history}}

main hall | location = 1-4-13 Marunouchi, Yonezawa City, [[Yamagata Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|37|54|33.5|N|140|6|14.7|E|region:JP-06_scale:25000_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Uesugi Shrine}} | festival Deities = Lord [[Uesugi Kenshin]] | Shrine Rank = Bekkaku Kanpeisha | established = Meiji 4 (1871) | festival = April 29 | deity = [[Uesugi Kenshin]] | Religious ceremony = | map = {{location map|Japan Yonezawa city#Japan Yamagata|label=Uesugi Shrine|position=center|width=200|float=center}} }} [[File:Uesugi kenshin.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Kenshin]] [[File:Uesugi-Yozan statue.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Yozan (located along the approach)]] '''Uesugi Shrine''' (うえすぎじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Yonezawa City]], [[Yamagata Prefecture]]. It is situated in [[Matsugasaki Park]] (the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]]) and enshrines [[Uesugi Kenshin]]. The former shrine Rank was [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. It is one of the shrines that enshrine clan founders, which became popular from the late [[Edo period]] to the early [[Meiji period]]. Uesugi Shrine (上杉神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Yonezawa, Yamagata]].{{Cite web|last=Organization|first=Japan National Tourism|title=Uesugi-jinja Shrine {{!}} Travel Japan (Japan National Tourism Organization)|url=https://www.japan.travel/en/spot/434/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=Travel Japan|language=en-us}}{{Cite web|last=山形県観光物産協会|first=公益社団法人|title=Uesugi Jinja Shrine｜What to See & Do｜STAY YAMAGATA|url=https://yamagatakanko.com/en/attractions/detail_1390.html|access-date=2023-04-07|website=STAY YAMAGATA|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=TOKYO|first=COPYRIGHT © TOHOKU ×|title=Uesugi-Jinja Shrine {{!}} TOHOKU x TOKYO (JAPAN)|url=https://www.tohokuandtokyo.org/spot_131/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=www.tohokuandtokyo.org|language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo shrine]] and is dedicated to the memory of [[Uesugi Kenshin]], a famous military leader in Japanese history. The shrine was built in 1876 on the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]], and it enshrines the spirit of [[Uesugi Kenshin]]. Every year in February, a snow lantern festival is held at the shrine where lanterns are carved out of snow to honor the memory of Uesugi Kenshin. It is a popular event that attracts many visitors. ==History== When [[Uesugi Kenshin]] suddenly died in [[Tensho]] 6 (1578) at [[Kasugayama Castle]] in [[Echigo Province]], his remains were enshrined in a Buddhist manner at the Fushikian within the castle. However, when [[Uesugi Kagekatsu]] was transferred to [[Aizu Domain]] and later to [[Yonezawa]] in [[Keicho]] 6 (1601), Kenshin's shrine was also moved to Yonezawa. After that, eleven temples, with [[Ho-onji Temple]] as the chief temple, alternated in conducting the rites at the second bailey of Yonezawa Castle. However, in the Meiji period, due to the [[Shinbutsu Bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and the [[Haijo-rei]] (abolition of castles decree), Kenshin's remains were moved from the castle to the [[Uesugi family mausoleum]], and Ho-onji Temple was relocated in front of the mausoleum for its protection. Additionally, to enshrine Kenshin's spirit in a Shinto manner, a monk from Daijoji Temple, the second of the eleven temples, renounced the monkhood and became a Shinto priest. The priest adopted the surname Daijoji and the family continues to serve as the chief priest to this day. At the same time, the shrine also enshrined [[Uesugi Yozan]], a notable lord who revived the Yonezawa Domain, and it became "Uesugi Shrine" in Yamagata Prefecture. On May 21, Meiji 9 (1876), the shrine building was relocated to its current location, the former inner palace site of Yonezawa Castle. On April 26, Meiji 35 (1902), it was Ranked as a [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. At this time, Yozan was transferred to a newly established subsidiary shrine, [[Matsugasaki Shrine]], and Uesugi Shrine once again exclusively enshrined Kenshin. In Taisho 8 (1919), a great fire destroyed the entire shrine precinct including the main hall. In Taisho 12 (1923), the current main hall and treasure hall "Keishoden" were reconstructed according to the design by Dr. [[Chuta Ito]] from Yonezawa City{{Cite web |url=https://yonezawa-kankou-navi.com/person/ito.html |title=Chuta Ito |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa City Tourism Campaign Promotion Council (Yonezawa City Tourism Section) |website=Yonezawa Tourism NAVI}}. ==Precincts== * main hall * Worship Hall * Keishoden (Treasure Hall) * Statue of Uesugi Kenshin located on the right side of the approach * Statue of Uesugi Yozan located along the approach * Statues of Uesugi Kagekatsu and Naoe Kanetsugu (Tenchijin statues) located along the approach * Kasuga Shrine * Fukutoku Inari Shrine * Memorial monument for the Akō incident, established by Tosuke Kimura File:UesugiShrine.JPG|Scene in the precincts (August 2009) File:Uesugi shrine 2.jpg|Approach ==Subsidiary Shrines== * [[Matsugasaki Shrine]] - Enshrines six deities including [[Uesugi Yozan]]. {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Uesugi Shrine | image = [[File:Uesugi shrine 1.jpg|250px|]]
main hall | location = 1-4-13 Marunouchi, Yonezawa City, [[Yamagata Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|37|54|33.5|N|140|6|14.7|E|region:JP-06_scale:25000_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Uesugi Shrine}} | festival Deities = Lord [[Uesugi Kenshin]] | Shrine Rank = Bekkaku Kanpeisha | established = Meiji 4 (1871) | festival = April 29 | deity = [[Uesugi Kenshin]] | Religious ceremony = | map = {{location map|Japan Yonezawa city#Japan Yamagata|label=Uesugi Shrine|position=center|width=200|float=center}} }} [[File:Uesugi kenshin.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Kenshin]] [[File:Uesugi-Yozan statue.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Yozan (located along the approach)]] '''Uesugi Shrine''' (うえすぎじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Yonezawa City]], [[Yamagata Prefecture]]. It is situated in [[Matsugasaki Park]] (the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]]) and enshrines [[Uesugi Kenshin]]. The former shrine Rank was [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. It is one of the shrines that enshrine clan founders, which became popular from the late [[Edo period]] to the early [[Meiji period]]. Uesugi Shrine (上杉神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Yonezawa, Yamagata]].{{Cite web|last=Organization|first=Japan National Tourism|title=Uesugi-jinja Shrine {{!}} Travel Japan (Japan National Tourism Organization)|url=https://www.japan.travel/en/spot/434/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=Travel Japan|language=en-us}}{{Cite web|last=山形県観光物産協会|first=公益社団法人|title=Uesugi Jinja Shrine｜What to See & Do｜STAY YAMAGATA|url=https://yamagatakanko.com/en/attractions/detail_1390.html|access-date=2023-04-07|website=STAY YAMAGATA|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=TOKYO|first=COPYRIGHT © TOHOKU ×|title=Uesugi-Jinja Shrine {{!}} TOHOKU x TOKYO (JAPAN)|url=https://www.tohokuandtokyo.org/spot_131/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=www.tohokuandtokyo.org|language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo shrine]] and is dedicated to the memory of [[Uesugi Kenshin]], a famous military leader in Japanese history. The shrine was built in 1876 on the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]], and it enshrines the spirit of [[Uesugi Kenshin]]. Every year in February, a snow lantern festival is held at the shrine where lanterns are carved out of snow to honor the memory of Uesugi Kenshin. It is a popular event that attracts many visitors. ==History== When [[Uesugi Kenshin]] suddenly died in [[Tensho]] 6 (1578) at [[Kasugayama Castle]] in [[Echigo Province]], his remains were enshrined in a Buddhist manner at the Fushikian within the castle. However, when [[Uesugi Kagekatsu]] was transferred to [[Aizu Domain]] and later to [[Yonezawa]] in [[Keicho]] 6 (1601), Kenshin's shrine was also moved to Yonezawa. After that, eleven temples, with [[Ho-onji Temple]] as the chief temple, alternated in conducting the rites at the second bailey of Yonezawa Castle. However, in the Meiji period, due to the [[Shinbutsu Bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and the [[Haijo-rei]] (abolition of castles decree), Kenshin's remains were moved from the castle to the [[Uesugi family mausoleum]], and Ho-onji Temple was relocated in front of the mausoleum for its protection. Additionally, to enshrine Kenshin's spirit in a Shinto manner, a monk from Daijoji Temple, the second of the eleven temples, renounced the monkhood and became a Shinto priest. The priest adopted the surname Daijoji and the family continues to serve as the chief priest to this day. At the same time, the shrine also enshrined [[Uesugi Yozan]], a notable lord who revived the Yonezawa Domain, and it became "Uesugi Shrine" in Yamagata Prefecture. On May 21, Meiji 9 (1876), the shrine building was relocated to its current location, the former inner palace site of Yonezawa Castle. On April 26, Meiji 35 (1902), it was Ranked as a [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. At this time, Yozan was transferred to a newly established subsidiary shrine, [[Matsugasaki Shrine]], and Uesugi Shrine once again exclusively enshrined Kenshin. In Taisho 8 (1919), a great fire destroyed the entire shrine precinct including the main hall. In Taisho 12 (1923), the current main hall and treasure hall "Keishoden" were reconstructed according to the design by Dr. [[Chuta Ito]] from Yonezawa City{{Cite web |url=https://yonezawa-kankou-navi.com/person/ito.html |title=Chuta Ito |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa City Tourism Campaign Promotion Council (Yonezawa City Tourism Section) |website=Yonezawa Tourism NAVI}}. ==Precincts== * main hall * Worship Hall * Keishoden (Treasure Hall) * Statue of Uesugi Kenshin located on the right side of the approach * Statue of Uesugi Yozan located along the approach * Statues of Uesugi Kagekatsu and Naoe Kanetsugu (Tenchijin statues) located along the approach * Kasuga Shrine * Fukutoku Inari Shrine * Memorial monument for the Akō incident, established by Tosuke Kimura File:UesugiShrine.JPG|Scene in the precincts (August 2009) File:Uesugi shrine 2.jpg|Approach ==Subsidiary Shrines== * [[Matsugasaki Shrine]] - Enshrines six deities including [[Uesugi Yozan]]. A statue of Yozan is located on the east side of the precincts (different in design from the statue on the approach to Uesugi Shrine). * [[Kasuga Shrine]] (in the precincts) - A shrine where Uesugi Yozan dedicated a pledge to study and train in martial arts, act justly, and award and punish fairly. * Fukutoku Inari Shrine (in the precincts) ==Major annual ceremony and Events== * [[January 1]] - Saitan festival and New Year's Prayers * [[January 15]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine fire rite * [[February 3]] - Setsubun festival * Second Saturday of February - Uesugi Snow Lantern festival Requiem Service * [[February 11]] - National Foundation Day Celebration * [[March 5]]–[[March 6]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine Old First Horse Day festival * Uesugi festival (April 28–May 3) ** [[April 28]] - Eve of the annual Grand festival ** [[April 29]] - annual Grand festival ** [[April 30]] - Matsugasaki Shrine festival ** [[April 30]] - Flower Offering festival ** [[May 1]] - Keishin Women's Association Spring Grand festival ** [[May 1]] - Carp Memorial Service ** [[May 2]] - Tea Offering festival ** [[May 3]] - Mikoshi Procession * Late May - Yozan Memorial festival (Rice Planting festival) * [[June 30]] - Great Purification ceremony * [[July 30]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine festival * [[September 25]] - Keizan Memorial Service * Last Saturday and Sunday of September - Matsugasaki Shrine Autumn Grand festival * Last Saturday and Sunday of September - Kasuga Shrine festival * Early October - Harvest festival * [[November 15]] - Shichi-Go-San Prayers * [[November 23]] - New Grain Thanksgiving festival * [[December 29]] - Old Talisman Burning ceremony * [[December 31]] - Great Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival ==Cultural Properties== [[File:Bishamonten (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|thumb|130px|right|Statue of Bishamonten (Late Heian period)]] [[File:Haramaki armour of Uesugi Kenshin.jpg|thumb|Iroiro-odoshi Haramaki with helmet and sleeve attachments, including black lacquer armor chest (allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin)]] '''[[Important Cultural Properties]]''' * Painted silk statue of Bishamonten * Purple damask golden mandala of the Two Realms * Painted silk statue of the Amida Triad (Koryo period, signed as Gen, second year of Zhida, 1309) (stolen in 1987) * Sword said to be made by Tomonari, with inscription on the front and the date of the third year of Kōan on the back * Sword with no inscription, with gold and silver inlay of Sanskrit characters and seven stars, with sheath decorated with the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac (allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin) * Sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Motoshige * Long sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Norikuni, with fittings * Long sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Katayama Ichimonji, with fittings * Long sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Katayama Ichimonji, with fittings * Spear inscribed "Made by Maeda" on December of the second year of Bunroku (10 items) * Iroiro-odoshi Haramaki with helmet and sleeve attachments, including black lacquer armor chest (allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin) * Garments allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin and Uesugi Kagekatsu (details provided later) * Light blue silk garment (allegedly used by Naoe Kanetsugu) * Collection of sutras including Wheel Mandala Box * Dark blue paper with gold characters of the Heart Sutra written by Emperor Go-Nara (stolen in 1987) * Sword signed "Sukemune," with leather-bound handle, used by Uesugi Kagekatsu (owned by Matsugasaki Shrine) * Ming court gifts to Uesugi Kagekatsu (1 hanging scroll) and Ming court garments (Sha Mao (expanded angle), rhinoceros horn belt, large red thread chestplate, green lining, shoes) These were split from the Important Cultural Properties "Garments allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin and Uesugi Kagekatsu" in 2018 (Notification No. 206 of the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, October 31, 2018) '''Other Cultural Properties''' * Gold small-laced light blue armor with accompanying helmet (used by Naoe Kanetsugu, known as the "Love" helmet)

{{-}} File:Amitabha Triad - Mahasthamaprapta (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Seishi Bodhisattva from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Amitabha Triad - Amitabha (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Amida Nyorai from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Amitabha Triad - a (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Kannon Bodhisattva from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Womb Realm Mandala (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|Purple Damask Golden Mudra Mandala of the Two Realms ==Carp Memorial== In Yonezawa, Uesugi Yozan encouraged the breeding and consumption of carp to provide a valuable protein source in the inland region. To promote the consumption of carp, "Carp Day" was established on [[May 1]], and since 1960, the Yonezawa Carp Merchants' Association has held the "Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival" to pray for business prosperity and memorialize the carp. During the festival, after the Shinto ceremony conducted by the chief priest of Uesugi Shrine, carp are released into the pond in the precincts. In the first year of the Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival, a monument to the carp memorial was erected in the precincts of Uesugi Shrine. The monument describes how, in 1810, a retainer of the Yonezawa Domain was sent to learn carp breeding methods in Edo's Honjo area and how, after his retirement, Uesugi Yozan established a nursery carp pond at Sankakukan and imported juvenile carp from Soma to sell as medicinal fish{{Cite web |url=https://www.yonezawa-np.jp/html/news/2023-S/20230502b.html |title=Carp Day (May 1), Carp Memorial festival at Uesugi Shrine |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa Nippo Digital |date=2023-05-02}}. ==Transportation Access== ===Rail=== * [[Ou Main Line]] (Yamagata Shinkansen) [[Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. * [[Yonesaka Line]] [[Minami-Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. ===Bus=== * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yamako Bus]] bound for [[Shirabu Onsen]], get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yonezawa City Community Bus]] City Loop Right Bus (blue bus) for 11 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From [[Sendai Station]], take the [[Express Bus]] Sendai-Yonezawa Line for 130 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. ===Road=== * Highway...From [[Tohoku Chuo Expressway]] [[Yonezawa Hachimanbara Interchange|Yonezawa Hachimanbara IC]], take [[Route 13]] towards Yamagata. It takes about 15 minutes by car from Route 13 Yonezawa Bypass. * National Route...From [[Kitakata]] use [[Route 121]], from [[Niigata City|Niigata]] use [[Route 113]]. * About 10 minutes by car from Yonezawa Station. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Related Books== * [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1112175/1/1 Compiled by Niroku Koshinjo, edited by Yonekichi Yamada, ''Seishi of Distinguished Shrine Bekkaku Kanpeisha,'' pp. 88-91, Niroku Koshinjo, 1935 (National Diet Library Digital Collection)] * Sukenari Azusa, Yoshihiko Umeda, editors and supervisors, ''Shinto Dictionary,'' Jinja Shinpōsha, [[1968]], p. 13 * Eiji Shirai, Masanori Toki, editors, ''Shrine Dictionary,'' [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], [[1979]], p. 52 ==See Also== {{Commonscat|Uesugi shrine}} * [[Chiura Obata]] {{Shinto temples}} {{Shinto-stub}} == References == {{Reflist}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ [[Category:translated pages without meta categories]]\n{{translated page|ja|上杉神社|version=98634141|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages without meta categories]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Uesugi Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]] }} [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]] [[en:Uesugi Shrine]] [[ja:上杉神社]]

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Uesugi Shrine | image = [[File:Uesugi shrine 1.jpg|250px|]]
main hall | location = 1-4-13 Marunouchi, Yonezawa City, [[Yamagata Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|37|54|33.5|N|140|6|14.7|E|region:JP-06_scale:25000_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Uesugi Shrine}} | festival Deities = Lord [[Uesugi Kenshin]] | Shrine Rank = Bekkaku Kanpeisha | established = Meiji 4 (1871) | festival = April 29 | deity = [[Uesugi Kenshin]] | Religious ceremony = | map = {{location map|Japan Yonezawa city#Japan Yamagata|label=Uesugi Shrine|position=center|width=200|float=center}} }} [[File:Uesugi kenshin.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Kenshin]] [[File:Uesugi-Yozan statue.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Yozan (located along the approach)]] '''Uesugi Shrine''' (うえすぎじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Yonezawa City]], [[Yamagata Prefecture]]. It is situated in [[Matsugasaki Park]] (the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]]) and enshrines [[Uesugi Kenshin]]. The former shrine Rank was [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. It is one of the shrines that enshrine clan founders, which became popular from the late [[Edo period]] to the early [[Meiji period]]. Uesugi Shrine (上杉神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Yonezawa, Yamagata]].{{Cite web|last=Organization|first=Japan National Tourism|title=Uesugi-jinja Shrine {{!}} Travel Japan (Japan National Tourism Organization)|url=https://www.japan.travel/en/spot/434/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=Travel Japan|language=en-us}}{{Cite web|last=山形県観光物産協会|first=公益社団法人|title=Uesugi Jinja Shrine｜What to See & Do｜STAY YAMAGATA|url=https://yamagatakanko.com/en/attractions/detail_1390.html|access-date=2023-04-07|website=STAY YAMAGATA|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=TOKYO|first=COPYRIGHT © TOHOKU ×|title=Uesugi-Jinja Shrine {{!}} TOHOKU x TOKYO (JAPAN)|url=https://www.tohokuandtokyo.org/spot_131/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=www.tohokuandtokyo.org|language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo shrine]] and is dedicated to the memory of [[Uesugi Kenshin]], a famous military leader in Japanese history. The shrine was built in 1876 on the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]], and it enshrines the spirit of [[Uesugi Kenshin]]. Every year in February, a snow lantern festival is held at the shrine where lanterns are carved out of snow to honor the memory of Uesugi Kenshin. It is a popular event that attracts many visitors. ==History== When [[Uesugi Kenshin]] suddenly died in [[Tensho]] 6 (1578) at [[Kasugayama Castle]] in [[Echigo Province]], his remains were enshrined in a Buddhist manner at the Fushikian within the castle. However, when [[Uesugi Kagekatsu]] was transferred to [[Aizu Domain]] and later to [[Yonezawa]] in [[Keicho]] 6 (1601), Kenshin's shrine was also moved to Yonezawa. After that, eleven temples, with [[Ho-onji Temple]] as the chief temple, alternated in conducting the rites at the second bailey of Yonezawa Castle. However, in the Meiji period, due to the [[Shinbutsu Bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and the [[Haijo-rei]] (abolition of castles decree), Kenshin's remains were moved from the castle to the [[Uesugi family mausoleum]], and Ho-onji Temple was relocated in front of the mausoleum for its protection. Additionally, to enshrine Kenshin's spirit in a Shinto manner, a monk from Daijoji Temple, the second of the eleven temples, renounced the monkhood and became a Shinto priest. The priest adopted the surname Daijoji and the family continues to serve as the chief priest to this day. At the same time, the shrine also enshrined [[Uesugi Yozan]], a notable lord who revived the Yonezawa Domain, and it became "Uesugi Shrine" in Yamagata Prefecture. On May 21, Meiji 9 (1876), the shrine building was relocated to its current location, the former inner palace site of Yonezawa Castle. On April 26, Meiji 35 (1902), it was Ranked as a [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. At this time, Yozan was transferred to a newly established subsidiary shrine, [[Matsugasaki Shrine]], and Uesugi Shrine once again exclusively enshrined Kenshin. In Taisho 8 (1919), a great fire destroyed the entire shrine precinct including the main hall. In Taisho 12 (1923), the current main hall and treasure hall "Keishoden" were reconstructed according to the design by Dr. [[Chuta Ito]] from Yonezawa City{{Cite web |url=https://yonezawa-kankou-navi.com/person/ito.html |title=Chuta Ito |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa City Tourism Campaign Promotion Council (Yonezawa City Tourism Section) |website=Yonezawa Tourism NAVI}}. ==Precincts== * main hall * Worship Hall * Keishoden (Treasure Hall) * Statue of Uesugi Kenshin located on the right side of the approach * Statue of Uesugi Yozan located along the approach * Statues of Uesugi Kagekatsu and Naoe Kanetsugu (Tenchijin statues) located along the approach * Kasuga Shrine * Fukutoku Inari Shrine * Memorial monument for the Akō incident, established by Tosuke Kimura File:UesugiShrine.JPG|Scene in the precincts (August 2009) File:Uesugi shrine 2.jpg|Approach ==Subsidiary Shrines== * [[Matsugasaki Shrine]] - Enshrines six deities including [[Uesugi Yozan]].
