{{-}} File:Amitabha Triad - Mahasthamaprapta (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Seishi Bodhisattva from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Amitabha Triad - Amitabha (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Amida Nyorai from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Amitabha Triad - a (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Kannon Bodhisattva from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Womb Realm Mandala (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|Purple Damask Golden Mudra Mandala of the Two Realms ==Carp Memorial== In Yonezawa, Uesugi Yozan encouraged the breeding and consumption of carp to provide a valuable protein source in the inland region. To promote the consumption of carp, "Carp Day" was established on [[:en:May 1|May 1]], and since 1960, the Yonezawa Carp Merchants' Association has held the "Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival" to pray for business prosperity and memorialize the carp. During the festival, after the Shinto ceremony conducted by the chief priest of Uesugi Shrine, carp are released into the pond in the precincts. In the first year of the Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival, a monument to the carp memorial was erected in the precincts of Uesugi Shrine. The monument describes how, in 1810, a retainer of the Yonezawa Domain was sent to learn carp breeding methods in Edo's Honjo area and how, after his retirement, Uesugi Yozan established a nursery carp pond at Sankakukan and imported juvenile carp from Soma to sell as medicinal fish{{Cite web |url=https://www.yonezawa-np.jp/html/news/2023-S/20230502b.html |title=Carp Day (May 1), Carp Memorial festival at Uesugi Shrine |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa Nippo Digital |date=2023-05-02}}. ==Transportation Access== ===Rail=== * [[:en:Ou Main Line|Ou Main Line]] (Yamagata Shinkansen) [[Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. * [[Yonesaka Line]] [[:en:Minami-Yonezawa Station|Minami-Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. ===Bus=== * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yamako Bus]] bound for [[Shirabu Onsen]], get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yonezawa City Community Bus]] City Loop Right Bus (blue bus) for 11 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From [[Sendai Station]], take the [[Express Bus]] Sendai-Yonezawa Line for 130 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. ===Road=== * Highway...From [[Tohoku Chuo Expressway]] [[Yonezawa Hachimanbara Interchange|Yonezawa Hachimanbara IC]], take [[Route 13]] towards Yamagata. It takes about 15 minutes by car from Route 13 Yonezawa Bypass. * National Route...From [[:en:Kitakata|Kitakata]] use [[Route 121]], from [[:en:Niigata City|Niigata]] use [[Route 113]]. * About 10 minutes by car from Yonezawa Station. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Related Books== * [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1112175/1/1 Compiled by Niroku Koshinjo, edited by Yonekichi Yamada, ''Seishi of Distinguished Shrine Bekkaku Kanpeisha,'' pp. 88-91, Niroku Koshinjo, 1935 (National Diet Library Digital Collection)] * Sukenari Azusa, Yoshihiko Umeda, editors and supervisors, ''Shinto Dictionary,'' Jinja Shinpōsha, [[:en:1968|1968]], p. 13 * Eiji Shirai, Masanori Toki, editors, ''Shrine Dictionary,'' [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], [[:en:1979|1979]], p. 52 ==See Also== {{Commonscat|Uesugi shrine}} * [[:en:Chiura Obata|Chiura Obata]] {{Shinto temples}} {{Shinto-stub}} == References == {{Reflist}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ [[Category:completion tier 1]] {{translated page|ja|上杉神社|version=98634141|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]]}} [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]] [[en:Uesugi Shrine]] [[ja:上杉神社]] [[Category:Uesugi Kagekatsu]] [[Category:Uesugi Kenshin]] [[Category:Uesugi Yozan]] [[Category:Itō Chūta]] [[Category:Bekkaku Kanpeisha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan in Yamagata prefecture]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Yamagata prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings in Yonezawa]] [[Category:History of Yonezawa]] [[Category:Yonezawa Domain]] [[Category:長尾上杉家]] {{Commons category|Uesugi shrine}} [[simple:Uesugi Shrine]] [[zh:上杉神社]] {{Commons category|Uesugi shrine}} [[simple:Uesugi Shrine]] [[zh:上杉神社]] [[Category:translated pages with valid en interwikis]]

{{-}} File:Amitabha Triad - Mahasthamaprapta (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Seishi Bodhisattva from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Amitabha Triad - Amitabha (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Amida Nyorai from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Amitabha Triad - a (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Kannon Bodhisattva from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Womb Realm Mandala (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|Purple Damask Golden Mudra Mandala of the Two Realms ==Carp Memorial== In Yonezawa, Uesugi Yozan encouraged the breeding and consumption of carp to provide a valuable protein source in the inland region. To promote the consumption of carp, "Carp Day" was established on [[:en:May 1|May 1]], and since 1960, the Yonezawa Carp Merchants' Association has held the "Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival" to pray for business prosperity and memorialize the carp. During the festival, after the Shinto ceremony conducted by the chief priest of Uesugi Shrine, carp are released into the pond in the precincts. In the first year of the Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival, a monument to the carp memorial was erected in the precincts of Uesugi Shrine. The monument describes how, in 1810, a retainer of the Yonezawa Domain was sent to learn carp breeding methods in Edo's Honjo area and how, after his retirement, Uesugi Yozan established a nursery carp pond at Sankakukan and imported juvenile carp from Soma to sell as medicinal fish{{Cite web |url=https://www.yonezawa-np.jp/html/news/2023-S/20230502b.html |title=Carp Day (May 1), Carp Memorial festival at Uesugi Shrine |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa Nippo Digital |date=2023-05-02}}. ==Transportation Access== ===Rail=== * [[:en:Ou Main Line|Ou Main Line]] (Yamagata Shinkansen) [[Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. * [[Yonesaka Line]] [[:en:Minami-Yonezawa Station|Minami-Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. ===Bus=== * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yamako Bus]] bound for [[Shirabu Onsen]], get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yonezawa City Community Bus]] City Loop Right Bus (blue bus) for 11 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From [[Sendai Station]], take the [[Express Bus]] Sendai-Yonezawa Line for 130 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. ===Road=== * Highway...From [[Tohoku Chuo Expressway]] [[Yonezawa Hachimanbara Interchange|Yonezawa Hachimanbara IC]], take [[Route 13]] towards Yamagata. It takes about 15 minutes by car from Route 13 Yonezawa Bypass. * National Route...From [[:en:Kitakata|Kitakata]] use [[Route 121]], from [[:en:Niigata City|Niigata]] use [[Route 113]]. * About 10 minutes by car from Yonezawa Station. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Related Books== * [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1112175/1/1 Compiled by Niroku Koshinjo, edited by Yonekichi Yamada, ''Seishi of Distinguished Shrine Bekkaku Kanpeisha,'' pp. 88-91, Niroku Koshinjo, 1935 (National Diet Library Digital Collection)] * Sukenari Azusa, Yoshihiko Umeda, editors and supervisors, ''Shinto Dictionary,'' Jinja Shinpōsha, [[:en:1968|1968]], p. 13 * Eiji Shirai, Masanori Toki, editors, ''Shrine Dictionary,'' [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], [[:en:1979|1979]], p. 52 ==See Also== {{Commonscat|Uesugi shrine}} * [[:en:Chiura Obata|Chiura Obata]] {{Shinto temples}} {{Shinto-stub}} == References == {{Reflist}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ [[Category:completion tier 1]] {{translated page|ja|上杉神社|version=98634141|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]]}} [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]] [[en:Uesugi Shrine]] [[ja:上杉神社]] [[Category:Uesugi Kagekatsu]] [[Category:Uesugi Kenshin]] [[Category:Uesugi Yozan]] [[Category:Itō Chūta]] [[Category:Bekkaku Kanpeisha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan in Yamagata prefecture]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Yamagata prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings in Yonezawa]] [[Category:History of Yonezawa]] [[Category:Yonezawa Domain]] [[Category:長尾上杉家]] {{Commons category|Uesugi shrine}} [[simple:Uesugi Shrine]] [[zh:上杉神社]] {{Commons category|Uesugi shrine}} [[simple:Uesugi Shrine]] [[zh:上杉神社]] [[Category:translated pages with valid en interwikis]]

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Uesugi Shrine | image = [[File:Uesugi shrine 1.jpg|250px|]]
main hall | location = 1-4-13 Marunouchi, Yonezawa City, [[:en:Yamagata Prefecture|Yamagata Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|37|54|33.5|N|140|6|14.7|E|region:JP-06_scale:25000_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Uesugi Shrine}} | festival Deities = Lord [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] | Shrine Rank = Bekkaku Kanpeisha | established = Meiji 4 (1871) | festival = April 29 | deity = [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] | Religious ceremony = | map = {{location map|Japan Yonezawa city#Japan Yamagata|label=Uesugi Shrine|position=center|width=200|float=center}} }} [[File:Uesugi kenshin.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Kenshin]] [[File:Uesugi-Yozan statue.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Yozan (located along the approach)]] '''Uesugi Shrine''' (うえすぎじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Yonezawa City]], [[:en:Yamagata Prefecture|Yamagata Prefecture]]. It is situated in [[Matsugasaki Park]] (the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]]) and enshrines [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]]. The former shrine Rank was [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. It is one of the shrines that enshrine clan founders, which became popular from the late [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]]. Uesugi Shrine (上杉神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Yonezawa, Yamagata]].{{Cite web|last=Organization|first=Japan National Tourism|title=Uesugi-jinja Shrine {{!}} Travel Japan (Japan National Tourism Organization)|url=https://www.japan.travel/en/spot/434/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=Travel Japan|language=en-us}}{{Cite web|last=山形県観光物産協会|first=公益社団法人|title=Uesugi Jinja Shrine｜What to See & Do｜STAY YAMAGATA|url=https://yamagatakanko.com/en/attractions/detail_1390.html|access-date=2023-04-07|website=STAY YAMAGATA|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=TOKYO|first=COPYRIGHT © TOHOKU ×|title=Uesugi-Jinja Shrine {{!}} TOHOKU x TOKYO (JAPAN)|url=https://www.tohokuandtokyo.org/spot_131/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=www.tohokuandtokyo.org|language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]] and is dedicated to the memory of [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]], a famous military leader in Japanese history. The shrine was built in 1876 on the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]], and it enshrines the spirit of [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]]. Every year in February, a snow lantern festival is held at the shrine where lanterns are carved out of snow to honor the memory of Uesugi Kenshin. It is a popular event that attracts many visitors. ==History== When [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] suddenly died in [[Tensho]] 6 (1578) at [[:en:Kasugayama Castle|Kasugayama Castle]] in [[:en:Echigo Province|Echigo Province]], his remains were enshrined in a Buddhist manner at the Fushikian within the castle. However, when [[:en:Uesugi Kagekatsu|Uesugi Kagekatsu]] was transferred to [[:en:Aizu Domain|Aizu Domain]] and later to [[Yonezawa]] in [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] 6 (1601), Kenshin's shrine was also moved to Yonezawa. After that, eleven temples, with [[Ho-onji Temple]] as the chief temple, alternated in conducting the rites at the second bailey of Yonezawa Castle. However, in the Meiji period, due to the [[Shinbutsu Bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and the [[Haijo-rei]] (abolition of castles decree), Kenshin's remains were moved from the castle to the [[Uesugi family mausoleum]], and Ho-onji Temple was relocated in front of the mausoleum for its protection. Additionally, to enshrine Kenshin's spirit in a Shinto manner, a monk from Daijoji Temple, the second of the eleven temples, renounced the monkhood and became a Shinto priest. The priest adopted the surname Daijoji and the family continues to serve as the chief priest to this day. At the same time, the shrine also enshrined [[:en:Uesugi Yozan|Uesugi Yozan]], a notable lord who revived the Yonezawa Domain, and it became "Uesugi Shrine" in Yamagata Prefecture. On May 21, Meiji 9 (1876), the shrine building was relocated to its current location, the former inner palace site of Yonezawa Castle. On April 26, Meiji 35 (1902), it was Ranked as a [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. At this time, Yozan was transferred to a newly established subsidiary shrine, [[Matsugasaki Shrine]], and Uesugi Shrine once again exclusively enshrined Kenshin. In Taisho 8 (1919), a great fire destroyed the entire shrine precinct including the main hall. In Taisho 12 (1923), the current main hall and treasure hall "Keishoden" were reconstructed according to the design by Dr. [[Chuta Ito]] from Yonezawa City{{Cite web |url=https://yonezawa-kankou-navi.com/person/ito.html |title=Chuta Ito |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa City Tourism Campaign Promotion Council (Yonezawa City Tourism Section) |website=Yonezawa Tourism NAVI}}. ==Precincts== * main hall * Worship Hall * Keishoden (Treasure Hall) * Statue of Uesugi Kenshin located on the right side of the approach * Statue of Uesugi Yozan located along the approach * Statues of Uesugi Kagekatsu and Naoe Kanetsugu (Tenchijin statues) located along the approach * Kasuga Shrine * Fukutoku Inari Shrine * Memorial monument for the Akō incident, established by Tosuke Kimura File:UesugiShrine.JPG|Scene in the precincts (August 2009) File:Uesugi shrine 2.jpg|Approach ==Subsidiary Shrines== * [[Matsugasaki Shrine]] - Enshrines six deities including [[:en:Uesugi Yozan|Uesugi Yozan]]. A statue of Yozan is located on the east side of the precincts (different in design from the statue on the approach to Uesugi Shrine). * [[Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Shrine]] (in the precincts) - A shrine where Uesugi Yozan dedicated a pledge to study and train in martial arts, act justly, and award and punish fairly. * Fukutoku Inari Shrine (in the precincts) ==Major annual ceremony and Events== * To promote the consumption of carp, "Carp Day" was established on [[:en:May 1|May 1]], and since 1960, the Yonezawa Carp Merchants' Association has held the "Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival" to pray for business prosperity and memorialize the carp. During the festival, after the Shinto ceremony conducted by the chief priest of Uesugi Shrine, carp are released into the pond in the precincts. In the first year of the Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival, a monument to the carp memorial was erected in the precincts of Uesugi Shrine. The monument describes how, in 1810, a retainer of the Yonezawa Domain was sent to learn carp breeding methods in Edo's Honjo area and how, after his retirement, Uesugi Yozan established a nursery carp pond at Sankakukan and imported juvenile carp from Soma to sell as medicinal fish{{Cite web |url=https://www.yonezawa-np.jp/html/news/2023-S/20230502b.html |title=Carp Day (May 1), Carp Memorial festival at Uesugi Shrine |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa Nippo Digital |date=2023-05-02}}. ==Transportation Access== ===Rail=== * [[:en:Ou Main Line|Ou Main Line]] (Yamagata Shinkansen) [[Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. * [[Yonesaka Line]] [[:en:Minami-Yonezawa Station|Minami-Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. ===Bus=== * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yamako Bus]] bound for [[Shirabu Onsen]], get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yonezawa City Community Bus]] City Loop Right Bus (blue bus) for 11 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From [[Sendai Station]], take the [[Express Bus]] Sendai-Yonezawa Line for 130 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. ===Road=== * Highway...From [[Tohoku Chuo Expressway]] [[Yonezawa Hachimanbara Interchange|Yonezawa Hachimanbara IC]], take [[Route 13]] towards Yamagata. {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Uesugi Shrine | image = [[File:Uesugi shrine 1.jpg|250px|]]
main hall | location = 1-4-13 Marunouchi, Yonezawa City, [[:en:Yamagata Prefecture|Yamagata Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|37|54|33.5|N|140|6|14.7|E|region:JP-06_scale:25000_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Uesugi Shrine}} | festival Deities = Lord [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] | Shrine Rank = Bekkaku Kanpeisha | established = Meiji 4 (1871) | festival = April 29 | deity = [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] | Religious ceremony = | map = {{location map|Japan Yonezawa city#Japan Yamagata|label=Uesugi Shrine|position=center|width=200|float=center}} }} [[File:Uesugi kenshin.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Kenshin]] [[File:Uesugi-Yozan statue.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Yozan (located along the approach)]] '''Uesugi Shrine''' (うえすぎじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Yonezawa City]], [[:en:Yamagata Prefecture|Yamagata Prefecture]]. It is situated in [[Matsugasaki Park]] (the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]]) and enshrines [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]]. The former shrine Rank was [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. It is one of the shrines that enshrine clan founders, which became popular from the late [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]]. Uesugi Shrine (上杉神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Yonezawa, Yamagata]].{{Cite web|last=Organization|first=Japan National Tourism|title=Uesugi-jinja Shrine {{!}} Travel Japan (Japan National Tourism Organization)|url=https://www.japan.travel/en/spot/434/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=Travel Japan|language=en-us}}{{Cite web|last=山形県観光物産協会|first=公益社団法人|title=Uesugi Jinja Shrine｜What to See & Do｜STAY YAMAGATA|url=https://yamagatakanko.com/en/attractions/detail_1390.html|access-date=2023-04-07|website=STAY YAMAGATA|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=TOKYO|first=COPYRIGHT © TOHOKU ×|title=Uesugi-Jinja Shrine {{!}} TOHOKU x TOKYO (JAPAN)|url=https://www.tohokuandtokyo.org/spot_131/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=www.tohokuandtokyo.org|language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]] and is dedicated to the memory of [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]], a famous military leader in Japanese history. The shrine was built in 1876 on the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]], and it enshrines the spirit of [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]]. Every year in February, a snow lantern festival is held at the shrine where lanterns are carved out of snow to honor the memory of Uesugi Kenshin. It is a popular event that attracts many visitors. ==History== When [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] suddenly died in [[Tensho]] 6 (1578) at [[:en:Kasugayama Castle|Kasugayama Castle]] in [[:en:Echigo Province|Echigo Province]], his remains were enshrined in a Buddhist manner at the Fushikian within the castle. However, when [[:en:Uesugi Kagekatsu|Uesugi Kagekatsu]] was transferred to [[:en:Aizu Domain|Aizu Domain]] and later to [[Yonezawa]] in [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] 6 (1601), Kenshin's shrine was also moved to Yonezawa. After that, eleven temples, with [[Ho-onji Temple]] as the chief temple, alternated in conducting the rites at the second bailey of Yonezawa Castle. However, in the Meiji period, due to the [[Shinbutsu Bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and the [[Haijo-rei]] (abolition of castles decree), Kenshin's remains were moved from the castle to the [[Uesugi family mausoleum]], and Ho-onji Temple was relocated in front of the mausoleum for its protection. Additionally, to enshrine Kenshin's spirit in a Shinto manner, a monk from Daijoji Temple, the second of the eleven temples, renounced the monkhood and became a Shinto priest. The priest adopted the surname Daijoji and the family continues to serve as the chief priest to this day. At the same time, the shrine also enshrined [[:en:Uesugi Yozan|Uesugi Yozan]], a notable lord who revived the Yonezawa Domain, and it became "Uesugi Shrine" in Yamagata Prefecture. On May 21, Meiji 9 (1876), the shrine building was relocated to its current location, the former inner palace site of Yonezawa Castle. On April 26, Meiji 35 (1902), it was Ranked as a [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. At this time, Yozan was transferred to a newly established subsidiary shrine, [[Matsugasaki Shrine]], and Uesugi Shrine once again exclusively enshrined Kenshin. In Taisho 8 (1919), a great fire destroyed the entire shrine precinct including the main hall. In Taisho 12 (1923), the current main hall and treasure hall "Keishoden" were reconstructed according to the design by Dr. [[Chuta Ito]] from Yonezawa City{{Cite web |url=https://yonezawa-kankou-navi.com/person/ito.html |title=Chuta Ito |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa City Tourism Campaign Promotion Council (Yonezawa City Tourism Section) |website=Yonezawa Tourism NAVI}}. ==Precincts== * main hall * Worship Hall * Keishoden (Treasure Hall) * Statue of Uesugi Kenshin located on the right side of the approach * Statue of Uesugi Yozan located along the approach * Statues of Uesugi Kagekatsu and Naoe Kanetsugu (Tenchijin statues) located along the approach * Kasuga Shrine * Fukutoku Inari Shrine * Memorial monument for the Akō incident, established by Tosuke Kimura File:UesugiShrine.JPG|Scene in the precincts (August 2009) File:Uesugi shrine 2.jpg|Approach ==Subsidiary Shrines== * [[Matsugasaki Shrine]] - Enshrines six deities including [[:en:Uesugi Yozan|Uesugi Yozan]]. A statue of Yozan is located on the east side of the precincts (different in design from the statue on the approach to Uesugi Shrine). * [[Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Shrine]] (in the precincts) - A shrine where Uesugi Yozan dedicated a pledge to study and train in martial arts, act justly, and award and punish fairly. * Fukutoku Inari Shrine (in the precincts) ==Major annual ceremony and Events== * [[:en:January 1|January 1]] - Saitan festival and New Year's Prayers * [[:en:January 15|January 15]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine fire rite * [[:en:February 3|February 3]] - Setsubun festival * Second Saturday of February - Uesugi Snow Lantern festival Requiem Service * [[:en:February 11|February 11]] - National Foundation Day Celebration * [[:en:March 5|March 5]]–[[:en:March 6|March 6]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine Old First Horse Day festival * Uesugi festival (April 28–May 3) ** [[:en:April 28|April 28]] - Eve of the annual Grand festival ** [[:en:April 29|April 29]] - annual Grand festival ** [[:en:April 30|April 30]] - Matsugasaki Shrine festival ** [[:en:April 30|April 30]] - Flower Offering festival ** [[:en:May 1|May 1]] - Keishin Women's Association Spring Grand festival ** [[:en:May 1|May 1]] - Carp Memorial Service ** [[:en:May 2|May 2]] - Tea Offering festival ** [[:en:May 3|May 3]] - Mikoshi Procession * Late May - Yozan Memorial festival (Rice Planting festival) * [[:en:June 30|June 30]] - Great Purification ceremony * [[:en:July 30|July 30]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine festival * [[September 25]] - Keizan Memorial Service * Last Saturday and Sunday of September - Matsugasaki Shrine Autumn Grand festival * Last Saturday and Sunday of September - Kasuga Shrine festival * Early October - Harvest festival * [[:en:November 15|November 15]] - Shichi-Go-San Prayers * [[:en:November 23|November 23]] - New Grain Thanksgiving festival * [[:en:December 29|December 29]] - Old Talisman Burning ceremony * [[:en:December 31|December 31]] - Great Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival ==Cultural Properties== [[File:Bishamonten (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|thumb|130px|right|Statue of Bishamonten (Late Heian period)]] [[File:Haramaki armour of Uesugi Kenshin.jpg|thumb|Iroiro-odoshi Haramaki with helmet and sleeve attachments, including black lacquer armor chest (allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin)]] '''[[:en:Important Cultural Properties|Important Cultural Properties]]''' * Painted silk statue of Bishamonten * Purple damask golden mandala of the Two Realms * Painted silk statue of the Amida Triad (Koryo period, signed as Gen, second year of Zhida, 1309) (stolen in 1987) * Sword said to be made by Tomonari, with inscription on the front and the date of the third year of Kōan on the back * Sword with no inscription, with gold and silver inlay of Sanskrit characters and seven stars, with sheath decorated with the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac (allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin) * Sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Motoshige * Long sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Norikuni, with fittings * Long sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Katayama Ichimonji, with fittings * Long sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Katayama Ichimonji, with fittings * Spear inscribed "Made by Maeda" on December of the second year of Bunroku (10 items) * Iroiro-odoshi Haramaki with helmet and sleeve attachments, including black lacquer armor chest (allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin) * Garments allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin and Uesugi Kagekatsu (details provided later) * Light blue silk garment (allegedly used by Naoe Kanetsugu) * Collection of sutras including Wheel Mandala Box * Dark blue paper with gold characters of the Heart Sutra written by Emperor Go-Nara (stolen in 1987) * Sword signed "Sukemune," with leather-bound handle, used by Uesugi Kagekatsu (owned by Matsugasaki Shrine) * Ming court gifts to Uesugi Kagekatsu (1 hanging scroll) and Ming court garments (Sha Mao (expanded angle), rhinoceros horn belt, large red thread chestplate, green lining, shoes) These were split from the Important Cultural Properties "Garments allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin and Uesugi Kagekatsu" in 2018 (Notification No. 206 of the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, October 31, 2018) '''Other Cultural Properties''' * Gold small-laced light blue armor with accompanying helmet (used by Naoe Kanetsugu, known as the "Love" helmet)

Uesugi Shrine (上杉神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Yonezawa, Yamagata]].{{Cite web|last=Organization|first=Japan National Tourism|title=Uesugi-jinja Shrine {{!}} Travel Japan (Japan National Tourism Organization)|url=https://www.japan.travel/en/spot/434/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=Travel Japan|language=en-us}}{{Cite web|last=山形県観光物産協会|first=公益社団法人|title=Uesugi Jinja Shrine｜What to See & Do｜STAY YAMAGATA|url=https://yamagatakanko.com/en/attractions/detail_1390.html|access-date=2023-04-07|website=STAY YAMAGATA|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=TOKYO|first=COPYRIGHT © TOHOKU ×|title=Uesugi-Jinja Shrine {{!}} TOHOKU x TOKYO (JAPAN)|url=https://www.tohokuandtokyo.org/spot_131/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=www.tohokuandtokyo.org|language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]] and is dedicated to the memory of [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]], a famous military leader in Japanese history. The shrine was built in 1876 on the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]], and it enshrines the spirit of [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]]. Every year in February, a snow lantern festival is held at the shrine where lanterns are carved out of snow to honor the memory of Uesugi Kenshin. It is a popular event that attracts many visitors. ==History== When [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] suddenly died in [[Tensho]] 6 (1578) at [[:en:Kasugayama Castle|Kasugayama Castle]] in [[:en:Echigo Province|Echigo Province]], his remains were enshrined in a Buddhist manner at the Fushikian within the castle. However, when [[:en:Uesugi Kagekatsu|Uesugi Kagekatsu]] was transferred to [[:en:Aizu Domain|Aizu Domain]] and later to [[Yonezawa]] in [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] 6 (1601), Kenshin's shrine was also moved to Yonezawa. After that, eleven temples, with [[Ho-onji Temple]] as the chief temple, alternated in conducting the rites at the second bailey of Yonezawa Castle. However, in the Meiji period, due to the [[Shinbutsu Bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and the [[Haijo-rei]] (abolition of castles decree), Kenshin's remains were moved from the castle to the [[Uesugi family mausoleum]], and Ho-onji Temple was relocated in front of the mausoleum for its protection. Additionally, to enshrine Kenshin's spirit in a Shinto manner, a monk from Daijoji Temple, the second of the eleven temples, renounced the monkhood and became a Shinto priest. The priest adopted the surname Daijoji and the family continues to serve as the chief priest to this day. At this time, Yozan was transferred to a newly established subsidiary shrine, [[Matsugasaki Shrine]], and Uesugi Shrine once again exclusively enshrined Kenshin. In Taisho 8 (1919), a great fire destroyed the entire shrine precinct including the main hall. {{-}} File:Amitabha Triad - Mahasthamaprapta (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Seishi Bodhisattva from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Amitabha Triad - Amitabha (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Amida Nyorai from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Amitabha Triad - a (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Kannon Bodhisattva from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Womb Realm Mandala (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|Purple Damask Golden Mudra Mandala of the Two Realms ==Carp Memorial== In Yonezawa, Uesugi Yozan encouraged the breeding and consumption of carp to provide a valuable protein source in the inland region. To promote the consumption of carp, "Carp Day" was established on [[:en:May 1|May 1]], and since 1960, the Yonezawa Carp Merchants' Association has held the "Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival" to pray for business prosperity and memorialize the carp. During the festival, after the Shinto ceremony conducted by the chief priest of Uesugi Shrine, carp are released into the pond in the precincts. In the first year of the Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival, a monument to the carp memorial was erected in the precincts of Uesugi Shrine. The monument describes how, in 1810, a retainer of the Yonezawa Domain was sent to learn carp breeding methods in Edo's Honjo area and how, after his retirement, Uesugi Yozan established a nursery carp pond at Sankakukan and imported juvenile carp from Soma to sell as medicinal fish{{Cite web |url=https://www.yonezawa-np.jp/html/news/2023-S/20230502b.html |title=Carp Day (May 1), Carp Memorial festival at Uesugi Shrine |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa Nippo Digital |date=2023-05-02}}. ==Transportation Access== ===Rail=== * [[:en:Ou Main Line|Ou Main Line]] (Yamagata Shinkansen) [[Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. * [[Yonesaka Line]] [[:en:Minami-Yonezawa Station|Minami-Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. ===Bus=== * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yamako Bus]] bound for [[Shirabu Onsen]], get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yonezawa City Community Bus]] City Loop Right Bus (blue bus) for 11 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From [[Sendai Station]], take the [[Express Bus]] Sendai-Yonezawa Line for 130 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. ===Road=== * Highway...From [[Tohoku Chuo Expressway]] [[Yonezawa Hachimanbara Interchange|Yonezawa Hachimanbara IC]], take [[Route 13]] towards Yamagata. It takes about 15 minutes by car from Route 13 Yonezawa Bypass. * National Route...From [[:en:Kitakata|Kitakata]] use [[:en:Route 121|Route 121]], from [[:en:Niigata City|Niigata]] use [[:en:Route 113|Route 113]]. * About 10 minutes by car from Yonezawa Station. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Related Books== * [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1112175/1/1 Compiled by Niroku Koshinjo, edited by Yonekichi Yamada, ''Seishi of Distinguished Shrine Bekkaku Kanpeisha,'' pp. 88-91, Niroku Koshinjo, 1935 (National Diet Library Digital Collection)] * Sukenari Azusa, Yoshihiko Umeda, editors and supervisors, ''Shinto Dictionary,'' Jinja Shinpōsha, [[:en:1968|1968]], p. 13 * Eiji Shirai, Masanori Toki, editors, ''Shrine Dictionary,'' [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], [[:en:1979|1979]], p. 52 ==See Also== {{Commonscat|Uesugi shrine}} * [[:en:Chiura Obata|Chiura Obata]] {{Shinto temples}} {{Shinto-stub}} == References == {{Reflist}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ [[Category:completion tier 1]] {{translated page|ja|上杉神社|version=98634141|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]]}} [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]] [[en:Uesugi Shrine]] [[ja:上杉神社]] [[Category:Uesugi Kagekatsu]] [[Category:Uesugi Kenshin]] [[Category:Uesugi Yozan]] [[Category:Itō Chūta]] [[Category:Bekkaku Kanpeisha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan in Yamagata prefecture]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Yamagata prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings in Yonezawa]] [[Category:History of Yonezawa]] [[Category:Yonezawa Domain]] [[Category:長尾上杉家]] {{Commons category|Uesugi shrine}} [[simple:Uesugi Shrine]] [[zh:上杉神社]] {{Commons category|Uesugi shrine}} [[simple:Uesugi Shrine]] [[zh:上杉神社]] [[Category:translated pages with valid en interwikis]]

To promote the consumption of carp, "Carp Day" was established on [[:en:May 1|May 1]], and since 1960, the Yonezawa Carp Merchants' Association has held the "Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival" to pray for business prosperity and memorialize the carp. During the festival, after the Shinto ceremony conducted by the chief priest of Uesugi Shrine, carp are released into the pond in the precincts. In the first year of the Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival, a monument to the carp memorial was erected in the precincts of Uesugi Shrine. The monument describes how, in 1810, a retainer of the Yonezawa Domain was sent to learn carp breeding methods in Edo's Honjo area and how, after his retirement, Uesugi Yozan established a nursery carp pond at Sankakukan and imported juvenile carp from Soma to sell as medicinal fish{{Cite web |url=https://www.yonezawa-np.jp/html/news/2023-S/20230502b.html |title=Carp Day (May 1), Carp Memorial festival at Uesugi Shrine |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa Nippo Digital |date=2023-05-02}}. ==Transportation Access== ===Rail=== * [[:en:Ou Main Line|Ou Main Line]] (Yamagata Shinkansen) [[Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. * [[Yonesaka Line]] [[:en:Minami-Yonezawa Station|Minami-Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. ===Bus=== * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yamako Bus]] bound for [[Shirabu Onsen]], get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yonezawa City Community Bus]] City Loop Right Bus (blue bus) for 11 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From [[Sendai Station]], take the [[Express Bus]] Sendai-Yonezawa Line for 130 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. ===Road=== * Highway...From [[Tohoku Chuo Expressway]] [[Yonezawa Hachimanbara Interchange|Yonezawa Hachimanbara IC]], take [[:en:Route 13|Route 13]] towards Yamagata. It takes about 15 minutes by car from Route 13 Yonezawa Bypass. * National Route...From [[:en:Kitakata|Kitakata]] use [[:en:Route 121|Route 121]], from [[:en:Niigata City|Niigata]] use [[:en:Route 113|Route 113]]. * About 10 minutes by car from Yonezawa Station. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Related Books== * [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1112175/1/1 Compiled by Niroku Koshinjo, edited by Yonekichi Yamada, ''Seishi of Distinguished Shrine Bekkaku Kanpeisha,'' pp. 88-91, Niroku Koshinjo, 1935 (National Diet Library Digital Collection)] * Sukenari Azusa, Yoshihiko Umeda, editors and supervisors, ''Shinto Dictionary,'' Jinja Shinpōsha, [[:en:1968|1968]], p. 13 * Eiji Shirai, Masanori Toki, editors, ''Shrine Dictionary,'' [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], [[:en:1979|1979]], p. 52 ==See Also== {{Commonscat|Uesugi shrine}} * [[:en:Chiura Obata|Chiura Obata]] {{Shinto temples}} {{Shinto-stub}} == References == {{Reflist}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ [[Category:completion tier 1]] {{translated page|ja|上杉神社|version=98634141|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]]}} [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]] [[en:Uesugi Shrine]] [[ja:上杉神社]] [[Category:Uesugi Kagekatsu]] [[Category:Uesugi Kenshin]] [[Category:Uesugi Yozan]] [[Category:Itō Chūta]] [[Category:Bekkaku Kanpeisha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan in Yamagata prefecture]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Yamagata prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings in Yonezawa]] [[Category:History of Yonezawa]] [[Category:Yonezawa Domain]] [[Category:長尾上杉家]] {{Commons category|Uesugi shrine}} [[simple:Uesugi Shrine]] [[zh:上杉神社]] {{Commons category|Uesugi shrine}} [[simple:Uesugi Shrine]] [[zh:上杉神社]] [[Category:translated pages with valid en interwikis]]

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Uesugi Shrine | image = [[File:Uesugi shrine 1.jpg|250px|]]
main hall | location = 1-4-13 Marunouchi, Yonezawa City, [[:en:Yamagata Prefecture|Yamagata Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|37|54|33.5|N|140|6|14.7|E|region:JP-06_scale:25000_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Uesugi Shrine}} | festival Deities = Lord [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] | Shrine Rank = Bekkaku Kanpeisha | established = Meiji 4 (1871) | festival = April 29 | deity = [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] | Religious ceremony = | map = {{location map|Japan Yonezawa city#Japan Yamagata|label=Uesugi Shrine|position=center|width=200|float=center}} }} [[File:Uesugi kenshin.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Kenshin]] [[File:Uesugi-Yozan statue.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Yozan (located along the approach)]] '''Uesugi Shrine''' (うえすぎじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Yonezawa City]], [[:en:Yamagata Prefecture|Yamagata Prefecture]]. It is situated in [[Matsugasaki Park]] (the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]]) and enshrines [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]]. The former shrine Rank was [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. It is one of the shrines that enshrine clan founders, which became popular from the late [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]]. Uesugi Shrine (上杉神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Yonezawa, Yamagata]].{{Cite web|last=Organization|first=Japan National Tourism|title=Uesugi-jinja Shrine {{!}} Travel Japan (Japan National Tourism Organization)|url=https://www.japan.travel/en/spot/434/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=Travel Japan|language=en-us}}{{Cite web|last=山形県観光物産協会|first=公益社団法人|title=Uesugi Jinja Shrine｜What to See & Do｜STAY YAMAGATA|url=https://yamagatakanko.com/en/attractions/detail_1390.html|access-date=2023-04-07|website=STAY YAMAGATA|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=TOKYO|first=COPYRIGHT © TOHOKU ×|title=Uesugi-Jinja Shrine {{!}} TOHOKU x TOKYO (JAPAN)|url=https://www.tohokuandtokyo.org/spot_131/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=www.tohokuandtokyo.org|language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]] and is dedicated to the memory of [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]], a famous military leader in Japanese history. The shrine was built in 1876 on the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]], and it enshrines the spirit of [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]]. Every year in February, a snow lantern festival is held at the shrine where lanterns are carved out of snow to honor the memory of Uesugi Kenshin. It is a popular event that attracts many visitors. ==History== When [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] suddenly died in [[Tensho]] 6 (1578) at [[:en:Kasugayama Castle|Kasugayama Castle]] in [[:en:Echigo Province|Echigo Province]], his remains were enshrined in a Buddhist manner at the Fushikian within the castle. However, when [[:en:Uesugi Kagekatsu|Uesugi Kagekatsu]] was transferred to [[:en:Aizu Domain|Aizu Domain]] and later to [[Yonezawa]] in [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] 6 (1601), Kenshin's shrine was also moved to Yonezawa. After that, eleven temples, with [[Ho-onji Temple]] as the chief temple, alternated in conducting the rites at the second bailey of Yonezawa Castle. However, in the Meiji period, due to the [[Shinbutsu Bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and the [[Haijo-rei]] (abolition of castles decree), Kenshin's remains were moved from the castle to the [[Uesugi family mausoleum]], and Ho-onji Temple was relocated in front of the mausoleum for its protection. Additionally, to enshrine Kenshin's spirit in a Shinto manner, a monk from Daijoji Temple, the second of the eleven temples, renounced the monkhood and became a Shinto priest. The priest adopted the surname Daijoji and the family continues to serve as the chief priest to this day. At the same time, the shrine also enshrined [[:en:Uesugi Yozan|Uesugi Yozan]], a notable lord who revived the Yonezawa Domain, and it became "Uesugi Shrine" in Yamagata Prefecture. On May 21, Meiji 9 (1876), the shrine building was relocated to its current location, the former inner palace site of Yonezawa Castle. On April 26, Meiji 35 (1902), it was Ranked as a [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. At this time, Yozan was transferred to a newly established subsidiary shrine, [[Matsugasaki Shrine]], and Uesugi Shrine once again exclusively enshrined Kenshin. In Taisho 8 (1919), a great fire destroyed the entire shrine precinct including the main hall. In Taisho 12 (1923), the current main hall and treasure hall "Keishoden" were reconstructed according to the design by Dr. [[Chuta Ito]] from Yonezawa City{{Cite web |url=https://yonezawa-kankou-navi.com/person/ito.html |title=Chuta Ito |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa City Tourism Campaign Promotion Council (Yonezawa City Tourism Section) |website=Yonezawa Tourism NAVI}}. ==Precincts== * main hall * Worship Hall * Keishoden (Treasure Hall) * Statue of Uesugi Kenshin located on the right side of the approach * Statue of Uesugi Yozan located along the approach * Statues of Uesugi Kagekatsu and Naoe Kanetsugu (Tenchijin statues) located along the approach * Kasuga Shrine * Fukutoku Inari Shrine * Memorial monument for the Akō incident, established by Tosuke Kimura File:UesugiShrine.JPG|Scene in the precincts (August 2009) File:Uesugi shrine 2.jpg|Approach ==Subsidiary Shrines== * [[Matsugasaki Shrine]] - Enshrines six deities including [[:en:Uesugi Yozan|Uesugi Yozan]]. A statue of Yozan is located on the east side of the precincts (different in design from the statue on the approach to Uesugi Shrine). * [[Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Shrine]] (in the precincts) - A shrine where Uesugi Yozan dedicated a pledge to study and train in martial arts, act justly, and award and punish fairly. * Fukutoku Inari Shrine (in the precincts) ==Major annual ceremony and Events== * [[:en:January 1|January 1]] - Saitan festival and New Year's Prayers * [[:en:January 15|January 15]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine fire rite * [[:en:February 3|February 3]] - Setsubun festival * Second Saturday of February - Uesugi Snow Lantern festival Requiem Service * [[:en:February 11|February 11]] - National Foundation Day Celebration * [[:en:March 5|March 5]]–[[:en:March 6|March 6]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine Old First Horse Day festival * Uesugi festival (April 28–May 3) ** [[:en:April 28|April 28]] - Eve of the annual Grand festival ** [[:en:April 29|April 29]] - annual Grand festival ** [[:en:April 30|April 30]] - Matsugasaki Shrine festival ** [[:en:April 30|April 30]] - Flower Offering festival ** [[:en:May 1|May 1]] - Keishin Women's Association Spring Grand festival ** [[:en:May 1|May 1]] - Carp Memorial Service ** [[:en:May 2|May 2]] - Tea Offering festival ** [[:en:May 3|May 3]] - Mikoshi Procession * Late May - Yozan Memorial festival (Rice Planting festival) * [[:en:June 30|June 30]] - Great Purification ceremony * [[:en:July 30|July 30]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine festival * [[September 25]] - Keizan Memorial Service * Last Saturday and Sunday of September - Matsugasaki Shrine Autumn Grand festival * Last Saturday and Sunday of September - Kasuga Shrine festival * Early October - Harvest festival * [[:en:November 15|November 15]] - Shichi-Go-San Prayers * [[:en:November 23|November 23]] - New Grain Thanksgiving festival * [[:en:December 29|December 29]] - Old Talisman Burning ceremony * [[:en:December 31|December 31]] - Great Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival ==Cultural Properties== [[File:Bishamonten (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|thumb|130px|right|Statue of Bishamonten (Late Heian period)]] [[File:Haramaki armour of Uesugi The monument describes how, in 1810, a retainer of the Yonezawa Domain was sent to learn carp breeding methods in Edo's Honjo area and how, after his retirement, Uesugi Yozan established a nursery carp pond at Sankakukan and imported juvenile carp from Soma to sell as medicinal fish{{Cite web |url=https://www.yonezawa-np.jp/html/news/2023-S/20230502b.html |title=Carp Day (May 1), Carp Memorial festival at Uesugi Shrine |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa Nippo Digital |date=2023-05-02}}. ==Transportation Access== ===Rail=== * [[:en:Ou Main Line|Ou Main Line]] (Yamagata Shinkansen) [[Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. * [[:en:Yonesaka Line|Yonesaka Line]] [[:en:Minami-Yonezawa Station|Minami-Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. ===Bus=== * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yamako Bus]] bound for [[Shirabu Onsen]], get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yonezawa City Community Bus]] City Loop Right Bus (blue bus) for 11 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From [[Sendai Station]], take the [[Express Bus]] Sendai-Yonezawa Line for 130 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. ===Road=== * Highway...From [[Tohoku Chuo Expressway]] [[Yonezawa Hachimanbara Interchange|Yonezawa Hachimanbara IC]], take [[:en:Route 13|Route 13]] towards Yamagata. It takes about 15 minutes by car from Route 13 Yonezawa Bypass. * National Route...From [[:en:Kitakata|Kitakata]] use [[:en:Route 121|Route 121]], from [[:en:Niigata City|Niigata]] use [[:en:Route 113|Route 113]]. * About 10 minutes by car from Yonezawa Station. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Related Books== * [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1112175/1/1 Compiled by Niroku Koshinjo, edited by Yonekichi Yamada, ''Seishi of Distinguished Shrine Bekkaku Kanpeisha,'' pp. 88-91, Niroku Koshinjo, 1935 (National Diet Library Digital Collection)] * Sukenari Azusa, Yoshihiko Umeda, editors and supervisors, ''Shinto Dictionary,'' Jinja Shinpōsha, [[:en:1968|1968]], p. 13 * Eiji Shirai, Masanori Toki, editors, ''Shrine Dictionary,'' [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], [[:en:1979|1979]], p. 52 ==See Also== {{Commonscat|Uesugi shrine}} * [[:en:Chiura Obata|Chiura Obata]] {{Shinto temples}} {{Shinto-stub}} == References == {{Reflist}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ [[Category:completion tier 1]] {{translated page|ja|上杉神社|version=98634141|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]]}} [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]] [[en:Uesugi Shrine]] [[ja:上杉神社]] [[Category:Uesugi Kagekatsu]] [[Category:Uesugi Kenshin]] [[Category:Uesugi Yozan]] [[Category:Itō Chūta]] [[Category:Bekkaku Kanpeisha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan in Yamagata prefecture]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Yamagata prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings in Yonezawa]] [[Category:History of Yonezawa]] [[Category:Yonezawa Domain]] [[Category:長尾上杉家]] {{Commons category|Uesugi shrine}} [[simple:Uesugi Shrine]] [[zh:上杉神社]] {{Commons category|Uesugi shrine}} [[simple:Uesugi Shrine]] [[zh:上杉神社]] [[Category:translated pages with valid en interwikis]]

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Uesugi Shrine | image = [[File:Uesugi shrine 1.jpg|250px|]]
main hall | location = 1-4-13 Marunouchi, Yonezawa City, [[:en:Yamagata Prefecture|Yamagata Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|37|54|33.5|N|140|6|14.7|E|region:JP-06_scale:25000_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Uesugi Shrine}} | festival Deities = Lord [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] | Shrine Rank = Bekkaku Kanpeisha | established = Meiji 4 (1871) | festival = April 29 | deity = [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] | Religious ceremony = | map = {{location map|Japan Yonezawa city#Japan Yamagata|label=Uesugi Shrine|position=center|width=200|float=center}} }} [[File:Uesugi kenshin.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Kenshin]] [[File:Uesugi-Yozan statue.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Yozan (located along the approach)]] '''Uesugi Shrine''' (うえすぎじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Yonezawa City]], [[:en:Yamagata Prefecture|Yamagata Prefecture]]. It is situated in [[Matsugasaki Park]] (the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]]) and enshrines [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]]. The former shrine Rank was [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. It is one of the shrines that enshrine clan founders, which became popular from the late [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]]. Uesugi Shrine (上杉神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Yonezawa, Yamagata]].{{Cite web|last=Organization|first=Japan National Tourism|title=Uesugi-jinja Shrine {{!}} Travel Japan (Japan National Tourism Organization)|url=https://www.japan.travel/en/spot/434/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=Travel Japan|language=en-us}}{{Cite web|last=山形県観光物産協会|first=公益社団法人|title=Uesugi Jinja Shrine｜What to See & Do｜STAY YAMAGATA|url=https://yamagatakanko.com/en/attractions/detail_1390.html|access-date=2023-04-07|website=STAY YAMAGATA|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=TOKYO|first=COPYRIGHT © TOHOKU ×|title=Uesugi-Jinja Shrine {{!}} TOHOKU x TOKYO (JAPAN)|url=https://www.tohokuandtokyo.org/spot_131/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=www.tohokuandtokyo.org|language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]] and is dedicated to the memory of [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]], a famous military leader in Japanese history. The shrine was built in 1876 on the site of [[Yonezawa Castle]], and it enshrines the spirit of [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]]. Every year in February, a snow lantern festival is held at the shrine where lanterns are carved out of snow to honor the memory of Uesugi Kenshin. It is a popular event that attracts many visitors. ==History== When [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] suddenly died in [[Tensho]] 6 (1578) at [[:en:Kasugayama Castle|Kasugayama Castle]] in [[:en:Echigo Province|Echigo Province]], his remains were enshrined in a Buddhist manner at the Fushikian within the castle. However, when [[:en:Uesugi Kagekatsu|Uesugi Kagekatsu]] was transferred to [[:en:Aizu Domain|Aizu Domain]] and later to [[:en:Yonezawa|Yonezawa]] in [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] 6 (1601), Kenshin's shrine was also moved to Yonezawa. After that, eleven temples, with [[Ho-onji Temple]] as the chief temple, alternated in conducting the rites at the second bailey of Yonezawa Castle. However, in the Meiji period, due to the [[Shinbutsu Bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and the [[Haijo-rei]] (abolition of castles decree), Kenshin's remains were moved from the castle to the [[Uesugi family mausoleum]], and Ho-onji Temple was relocated in front of the mausoleum for its protection. Additionally, to enshrine Kenshin's spirit in a Shinto manner, a monk from Daijoji Temple, the second of the eleven temples, renounced the monkhood and became a Shinto priest. The priest adopted the surname Daijoji and the family continues to serve as the chief priest to this day. At the same time, the shrine also enshrined [[:en:Uesugi Yozan|Uesugi Yozan]], a notable lord who revived the Yonezawa Domain, and it became "Uesugi Shrine" in Yamagata Prefecture. On May 21, Meiji 9 (1876), the shrine building was relocated to its current location, the former inner palace site of Yonezawa Castle. On April 26, Meiji 35 (1902), it was Ranked as a [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. At this time, Yozan was transferred to a newly established subsidiary shrine, [[Matsugasaki Shrine]], and Uesugi Shrine once again exclusively enshrined Kenshin. In Taisho 8 (1919), a great fire destroyed the entire shrine precinct including the main hall. In Taisho 12 (1923), the current main hall and treasure hall "Keishoden" were reconstructed according to the design by Dr. [[Chuta Ito]] from Yonezawa City{{Cite web |url=https://yonezawa-kankou-navi.com/person/ito.html |title=Chuta Ito |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa City Tourism Campaign Promotion Council (Yonezawa City Tourism Section) |website=Yonezawa Tourism NAVI}}. ==Precincts== * main hall * Worship Hall * Keishoden (Treasure Hall) * Statue of Uesugi Kenshin located on the right side of the approach * Statue of Uesugi Yozan located along the approach * Statues of Uesugi Kagekatsu and Naoe Kanetsugu (Tenchijin statues) located along the approach * Kasuga Shrine * Fukutoku Inari Shrine * Memorial monument for the Akō incident, established by Tosuke Kimura File:UesugiShrine.JPG|Scene in the precincts (August 2009) File:Uesugi shrine 2.jpg|Approach ==Subsidiary Shrines== * [[Matsugasaki Shrine]] - Enshrines six deities including [[:en:Uesugi Yozan|Uesugi Yozan]]. A statue of Yozan is located on the east side of the precincts (different in design from the statue on the approach to Uesugi Shrine). * [[Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Shrine]] (in the precincts) - A shrine where Uesugi Yozan dedicated a pledge to study and train in martial arts, act justly, and award and punish fairly. * Fukutoku Inari Shrine (in the precincts) ==Major annual ceremony and Events== * [[:en:January 1|January 1]] - Saitan festival and New Year's Prayers * [[:en:January 15|January 15]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine fire rite * [[:en:February 3|February 3]] - Setsubun festival * Second Saturday of February - Uesugi Snow Lantern festival Requiem Service * [[:en:February 11|February 11]] - National Foundation Day Celebration * [[:en:March 5|March 5]]–[[:en:March 6|March 6]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine Old First Horse Day festival * Uesugi festival (April 28–May 3) ** [[:en:April 28|April 28]] - Eve of the annual Grand festival ** [[:en:April 29|April 29]] - annual Grand festival ** [[:en:April 30|April 30]] - Matsugasaki Shrine festival ** [[:en:April 30|April 30]] - Flower Offering festival ** [[:en:May 1|May 1]] - Keishin Women's Association Spring Grand festival ** [[:en:May 1|May 1]] - Carp Memorial Service ** [[:en:May 2|May 2]] - Tea Offering festival ** [[:en:May 3|May 3]] - Mikoshi Procession * Late May - Yozan Memorial festival (Rice Planting festival) * [[:en:June 30|June 30]] - Great Purification ceremony * [[:en:July 30|July 30]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine festival * [[September 25]] - Keizan Memorial Service * Last Saturday and Sunday of September - Matsugasaki Shrine Autumn Grand festival * Last Saturday and Sunday of September - Kasuga Shrine festival * Early October - Harvest festival * [[:en:November 15|November 15]] - Shichi-Go-San Prayers * [[:en:November 23|November 23]] - New Grain Thanksgiving festival * [[:en:December 29|December 29]] - Old Talisman Burning ceremony * [[:en:December 31|December 31]] - Great Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival ==Cultural Properties== [[File:Bishamonten (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|thumb|130px|right|Statue of Bishamonten (Late Heian period)]] [[File:Haramaki armour of Uesugi To promote the consumption of carp, "Carp Day" was established on [[:en:May 1|May 1]], and since 1960, the Yonezawa Carp Merchants' Association has held the "Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival" to pray for business prosperity and memorialize the carp. During the festival, after the Shinto ceremony conducted by the chief priest of Uesugi Shrine, carp are released into the pond in the precincts. In the first year of the Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival, a monument to the carp memorial was erected in the precincts of Uesugi Shrine. It is a popular event that attracts many visitors. ==History== When [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] suddenly died in [[Tensho]] 6 (1578) at [[:en:Kasugayama Castle|Kasugayama Castle]] in [[:en:Echigo Province|Echigo Province]], his remains were enshrined in a Buddhist manner at the Fushikian within the castle. However, when [[:en:Uesugi Kagekatsu|Uesugi Kagekatsu]] was transferred to [[:en:Aizu Domain|Aizu Domain]] and later to [[:en:Yonezawa|Yonezawa]] in [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] 6 (1601), Kenshin's shrine was also moved to Yonezawa. After that, eleven temples, with [[Ho-onji Temple]] as the chief temple, alternated in conducting the rites at the second bailey of Yonezawa Castle. However, in the Meiji period, due to the [[Shinbutsu Bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and the [[Haijo-rei]] (abolition of castles decree), Kenshin's remains were moved from the castle to the [[Uesugi family mausoleum]], and Ho-onji Temple was relocated in front of the mausoleum for its protection. Additionally, to enshrine Kenshin's spirit in a Shinto manner, a monk from Daijoji Temple, the second of the eleven temples, renounced the monkhood and became a Shinto priest. The priest adopted the surname Daijoji and the family continues to serve as the chief priest to this day. At the same time, the shrine also enshrined [[:en:Uesugi Yozan|Uesugi Yozan]], a notable lord who revived the Yonezawa Domain, and it became "Uesugi Shrine" in Yamagata Prefecture. On May 21, Meiji 9 (1876), the shrine building was relocated to its current location, the former inner palace site of Yonezawa Castle. On April 26, Meiji 35 (1902), it was Ranked as a [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. At this time, Yozan was transferred to a newly established subsidiary shrine, [[Matsugasaki Shrine]], and Uesugi Shrine once again exclusively enshrined Kenshin. In Taisho 8 (1919), a great fire destroyed the entire shrine precinct including the main hall. In Taisho 12 (1923), the current main hall and treasure hall "Keishoden" were reconstructed according to the design by Dr. [[Chuta Ito]] from Yonezawa City{{Cite web |url=https://yonezawa-kankou-navi.com/person/ito.html |title=Chuta Ito |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa City Tourism Campaign Promotion Council (Yonezawa City Tourism Section) |website=Yonezawa Tourism NAVI}}. ==Precincts== * main hall * Worship Hall * Keishoden (Treasure Hall) * Statue of Uesugi Kenshin located on the right side of the approach * Statue of Uesugi Yozan located along the approach * Statues of Uesugi Kagekatsu and Naoe Kanetsugu (Tenchijin statues) located along the approach * Kasuga Shrine * Fukutoku Inari Shrine * Memorial monument for the Akō incident, established by Tosuke Kimura File:UesugiShrine.JPG|Scene in the precincts (August 2009) File:Uesugi shrine 2.jpg|Approach ==Subsidiary Shrines== * [[Matsugasaki Shrine]] - Enshrines six deities including [[:en:Uesugi Yozan|Uesugi Yozan]]. A statue of Yozan is located on the east side of the precincts (different in design from the statue on the approach to Uesugi Shrine). * [[Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Shrine]] (in the precincts) - A shrine where Uesugi Yozan dedicated a pledge to study and train in martial arts, act justly, and award and punish fairly. * Fukutoku Inari Shrine (in the precincts) ==Major annual ceremony and Events== * {{-}} File:Amitabha Triad - Mahasthamaprapta (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Seishi Bodhisattva from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Amitabha Triad - Amitabha (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Amida Nyorai from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Amitabha Triad - a (Uesugi Jinja).jpg|Statue of Kannon Bodhisattva from the Amida Triad (Koryo period) File:Womb Realm Mandala (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|Purple Damask Golden Mudra Mandala of the Two Realms ==Carp Memorial== In Yonezawa, Uesugi Yozan encouraged the breeding and consumption of carp to provide a valuable protein source in the inland region. To promote the consumption of carp, "Carp Day" was established on [[:en:May 1|May 1]], and since 1960, the Yonezawa Carp Merchants' Association has held the "Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival" to pray for business prosperity and memorialize the carp. During the festival, after the Shinto ceremony conducted by the chief priest of Uesugi Shrine, carp are released into the pond in the precincts. In the first year of the Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival, a monument to the carp memorial was erected in the precincts of Uesugi Shrine. The monument describes how, in 1810, a retainer of the Yonezawa Domain was sent to learn carp breeding methods in Edo's Honjo area and how, after his retirement, Uesugi Yozan established a nursery carp pond at Sankakukan and imported juvenile carp from Soma to sell as medicinal fish{{Cite web |url=https://www.yonezawa-np.jp/html/news/2023-S/20230502b.html |title=Carp Day (May 1), Carp Memorial festival at Uesugi Shrine |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa Nippo Digital |date=2023-05-02}}. ==Transportation Access== ===Rail=== * [[:en:Ou Main Line|Ou Main Line]] (Yamagata Shinkansen) [[Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. * [[:en:Yonesaka Line|Yonesaka Line]] [[:en:Minami-Yonezawa Station|Minami-Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. ===Bus=== * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yamako Bus]] bound for [[Shirabu Onsen]], get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yonezawa City Community Bus]] City Loop Right Bus (blue bus) for 11 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From [[Sendai Station]], take the [[Express Bus]] Sendai-Yonezawa Line for 130 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. ===Road=== * Highway...From [[Tohoku Chuo Expressway]] [[Yonezawa Hachimanbara Interchange|Yonezawa Hachimanbara IC]], take [[:en:Route 13|Route 13]] towards Yamagata. It takes about 15 minutes by car from Route 13 Yonezawa Bypass. * National Route...From [[:en:Kitakata|Kitakata]] use [[:en:Route 121|Route 121]], from [[:en:Niigata City|Niigata]] use [[:en:Route 113|Route 113]]. * About 10 minutes by car from Yonezawa Station. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Related Books== * [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1112175/1/1 Compiled by Niroku Koshinjo, edited by Yonekichi Yamada, ''Seishi of Distinguished Shrine Bekkaku Kanpeisha,'' pp. 88-91, Niroku Koshinjo, 1935 (National Diet Library Digital Collection)] * Sukenari Azusa, Yoshihiko Umeda, editors and supervisors, ''Shinto Dictionary,'' Jinja Shinpōsha, [[:en:1968|1968]], p. 13 * Eiji Shirai, Masanori Toki, editors, ''Shrine Dictionary,'' [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], [[:en:1979|1979]], p. 52 ==See Also== {{Commonscat|Uesugi shrine}} * [[:en:Chiura Obata|Chiura Obata]] {{Shinto temples}} {{Shinto-stub}} == References == {{Reflist}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ [[Category:completion tier 1]] {{translated page|ja|上杉神社|version=98634141|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]]}} [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]] [[en:Uesugi Shrine]] [[ja:上杉神社]] [[Category:Uesugi Kagekatsu]] [[Category:Uesugi Kenshin]] [[Category:Uesugi Yozan]] [[Category:Itō Chūta]] [[Category:Bekkaku Kanpeisha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan in Yamagata prefecture]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Yamagata prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings in Yonezawa]] [[Category:History of Yonezawa]] [[Category:Yonezawa Domain]] [[Category:長尾上杉家]] {{Commons category|Uesugi shrine}} [[simple:Uesugi Shrine]] [[zh:上杉神社]] {{Commons category|Uesugi shrine}} [[simple:Uesugi Shrine]] [[zh:上杉神社]] [[Category:translated pages with valid en interwikis]]

To promote the consumption of carp, "Carp Day" was established on [[:en:May 1|May 1]], and since 1960, the Yonezawa Carp Merchants' Association has held the "Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival" to pray for business prosperity and memorialize the carp. During the festival, after the Shinto ceremony conducted by the chief priest of Uesugi Shrine, carp are released into the pond in the precincts. In the first year of the Yonezawa Carp Memorial festival, a monument to the carp memorial was erected in the precincts of Uesugi Shrine. The monument describes how, in 1810, a retainer of the Yonezawa Domain was sent to learn carp breeding methods in Edo's Honjo area and how, after his retirement, Uesugi Yozan established a nursery carp pond at Sankakukan and imported juvenile carp from Soma to sell as medicinal fish{{Cite web |url=https://www.yonezawa-np.jp/html/news/2023-S/20230502b.html |title=Carp Day (May 1), Carp Memorial festival at Uesugi Shrine |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa Nippo Digital |date=2023-05-02}}. ==Transportation Access== ===Rail=== * [[:en:Ou Main Line|Ou Main Line]] (Yamagata Shinkansen) [[Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. * [[:en:Yonesaka Line|Yonesaka Line]] [[:en:Minami-Yonezawa Station|Minami-Yonezawa Station]], about 20 minutes on foot. ===Bus=== * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yamako Bus]] bound for [[Shirabu Onsen]], get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From Yonezawa Station, take the [[Yonezawa City Community Bus]] City Loop Right Bus (blue bus) for 11 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. * From [[Sendai Station]], take the [[Express Bus]] Sendai-Yonezawa Line for 130 minutes, get off at "Uesugi Shrine-mae," then walk for 3 minutes. ===Road=== * Highway...From [[Tohoku Chuo Expressway]] [[Yonezawa Hachimanbara Interchange|Yonezawa Hachimanbara IC]], take [[:en:Route 13|Route 13]] towards Yamagata. It takes about 15 minutes by car from Route 13 Yonezawa Bypass. * National Route...From [[:en:Kitakata|Kitakata]] use [[:en:Route 121|Route 121]], from [[:en:Niigata City|Niigata]] use [[:en:Route 113|Route 113]]. * About 10 minutes by car from Yonezawa Station. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Related Books== * [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1112175/1/1 Compiled by Niroku Koshinjo, edited by Yonekichi Yamada, ''Seishi of Distinguished Shrine Bekkaku Kanpeisha,'' pp. 88-91, Niroku Koshinjo, 1935 (National Diet Library Digital Collection)] * Sukenari Azusa, Yoshihiko Umeda, editors and supervisors, ''Shinto Dictionary,'' Jinja Shinpōsha, [[:en:1968|1968]], p. 13 * Eiji Shirai, Masanori Toki, editors, ''Shrine Dictionary,'' [[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], [[:en:1979|1979]], p. 52 ==See Also== {{Commonscat|Uesugi shrine}} * [[:en:Chiura Obata|Chiura Obata]] {{Shinto temples}} {{Shinto-stub}} == References == {{Reflist}} ]] {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ [[Category:completion tier 1]] {{translated page|ja|上杉神社|version=98634141|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]]}} [[sn:Uesugi Shrine]] [[en:Uesugi Shrine]] [[ja:上杉神社]] [[Category:Uesugi Kagekatsu]] [[Category:Uesugi Kenshin]] [[Category:Uesugi Yozan]] [[Category:Itō Chūta]] [[Category:Bekkaku Kanpeisha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan in Yamagata prefecture]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Yamagata Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Yamagata prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings in Yonezawa]] [[Category:History of Yonezawa]] [[Category:Yonezawa Domain]] [[Category:長尾上杉家]] {{Commons category|Uesugi shrine}} [[simple:Uesugi Shrine]] [[zh:上杉神社]] {{Commons category|Uesugi shrine}} [[simple:Uesugi Shrine]] [[zh:上杉神社]] [[Category:translated pages with valid en interwikis]]

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Uesugi Shrine | image = [[File:Uesugi shrine 1.jpg|250px|]]
main hall | location = 1-4-13 Marunouchi, Yonezawa City, [[:en:Yamagata Prefecture|Yamagata Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|37|54|33.5|N|140|6|14.7|E|region:JP-06_scale:25000_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Uesugi Shrine}} | festival Deities = Lord [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] | Shrine Rank = Bekkaku Kanpeisha | established = Meiji 4 (1871) | festival = April 29 | deity = [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] | Religious ceremony = | map = {{location map|Japan Yonezawa city#Japan Yamagata|label=Uesugi Shrine|position=center|width=200|float=center}} }} [[File:Uesugi kenshin.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Kenshin]] [[File:Uesugi-Yozan statue.jpg|thumbnail|150px|Statue of Uesugi Yozan (located along the approach)]] '''Uesugi Shrine''' (うえすぎじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Yonezawa City]], [[:en:Yamagata Prefecture|Yamagata Prefecture]]. It is situated in [[Matsugasaki Park]] (the site of [[:en:Yonezawa Castle|Yonezawa Castle]]) and enshrines [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]]. The former shrine Rank was [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. It is one of the shrines that enshrine clan founders, which became popular from the late [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji era]]. Uesugi Shrine (上杉神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[:en:Yonezawa, Yamagata|Yonezawa, Yamagata]].{{Cite web|last=Organization|first=Japan National Tourism|title=Uesugi-jinja Shrine {{!}} Travel Japan (Japan National Tourism Organization)|url=https://www.japan.travel/en/spot/434/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=Travel Japan|language=en-us}}{{Cite web|last=山形県観光物産協会|first=公益社団法人|title=Uesugi Jinja Shrine｜What to See & Do｜STAY YAMAGATA|url=https://yamagatakanko.com/en/attractions/detail_1390.html|access-date=2023-04-07|website=STAY YAMAGATA|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=TOKYO|first=COPYRIGHT © TOHOKU ×|title=Uesugi-Jinja Shrine {{!}} TOHOKU x TOKYO (JAPAN)|url=https://www.tohokuandtokyo.org/spot_131/|access-date=2023-04-07|website=www.tohokuandtokyo.org|language=en}} It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]] and is dedicated to the memory of [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]], a famous military leader in Japanese history. The shrine was built in 1876 on the site of [[:en:Yonezawa Castle|Yonezawa Castle]], and it enshrines the spirit of [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]]. Every year in February, a snow lantern festival is held at the shrine where lanterns are carved out of snow to honor the memory of Uesugi Kenshin. It is a popular event that attracts many visitors. ==History== When [[:en:Uesugi Kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] suddenly died in [[Tensho]] 6 (1578) at [[:en:Kasugayama Castle|Kasugayama Castle]] in [[:en:Echigo Province|Echigo Province]], his remains were enshrined in a Buddhist manner at the Fushikian within the castle. However, when [[:en:Uesugi Kagekatsu|Uesugi Kagekatsu]] was transferred to [[:en:Aizu Domain|Aizu Domain]] and later to [[:en:Yonezawa|Yonezawa]] in [[:en:Keicho|Keicho]] 6 (1601), Kenshin's shrine was also moved to Yonezawa. After that, eleven temples, with [[Ho-onji Temple]] as the chief temple, alternated in conducting the rites at the second bailey of Yonezawa Castle. However, in the Meiji period, due to the [[Shinbutsu Bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) and the [[Haijo-rei]] (abolition of castles decree), Kenshin's remains were moved from the castle to the [[Uesugi family mausoleum]], and Ho-onji Temple was relocated in front of the mausoleum for its protection. Additionally, to enshrine Kenshin's spirit in a Shinto manner, a monk from Daijoji Temple, the second of the eleven temples, renounced the monkhood and became a Shinto priest. The priest adopted the surname Daijoji and the family continues to serve as the chief priest to this day. At the same time, the shrine also enshrined [[:en:Uesugi Yozan|Uesugi Yozan]], a notable lord who revived the Yonezawa Domain, and it became "Uesugi Shrine" in Yamagata Prefecture. On May 21, Meiji 9 (1876), the shrine building was relocated to its current location, the former inner palace site of Yonezawa Castle. On April 26, Meiji 35 (1902), it was Ranked as a [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Bekkaku Kanpeisha]]. At this time, Yozan was transferred to a newly established subsidiary shrine, [[Matsugasaki Shrine]], and Uesugi Shrine once again exclusively enshrined Kenshin. In Taisho 8 (1919), a great fire destroyed the entire shrine precinct including the main hall. In Taisho 12 (1923), the current main hall and treasure hall "Keishoden" were reconstructed according to the design by Dr. [[Chuta Ito]] from Yonezawa City{{Cite web |url=https://yonezawa-kankou-navi.com/person/ito.html |title=Chuta Ito |access-date=2023-12-28 |publisher=Yonezawa City Tourism Campaign Promotion Council (Yonezawa City Tourism Section) |website=Yonezawa Tourism NAVI}}. ==Precincts== * main hall * Worship Hall * Keishoden (Treasure Hall) * Statue of Uesugi Kenshin located on the right side of the approach * Statue of Uesugi Yozan located along the approach * Statues of Uesugi Kagekatsu and Naoe Kanetsugu (Tenchijin statues) located along the approach * Kasuga Shrine * Fukutoku Inari Shrine * Memorial monument for the Akō incident, established by Tosuke Kimura File:UesugiShrine.JPG|Scene in the precincts (August 2009) File:Uesugi shrine 2.jpg|Approach ==Subsidiary Shrines== * [[Matsugasaki Shrine]] - Enshrines six deities including [[:en:Uesugi Yozan|Uesugi Yozan]]. A statue of Yozan is located on the east side of the precincts (different in design from the statue on the approach to Uesugi Shrine). * [[Kasuga-taisha|Kasuga Shrine]] (in the precincts) - A shrine where Uesugi Yozan dedicated a pledge to study and train in martial arts, act justly, and award and punish fairly. * Fukutoku Inari Shrine (in the precincts) ==Major annual ceremony and Events== * [[:en:January 1|January 1]] - Saitan festival and New Year's Prayers * [[:en:January 15|January 15]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine fire rite * [[:en:February 3|February 3]] - Setsubun festival * Second Saturday of February - Uesugi Snow Lantern festival Requiem Service * [[:en:February 11|February 11]] - National Foundation Day Celebration * [[:en:March 5|March 5]]–[[:en:March 6|March 6]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine Old First Horse Day festival * Uesugi festival (April 28–May 3) ** [[:en:April 28|April 28]] - Eve of the annual Grand festival ** [[:en:April 29|April 29]] - annual Grand festival ** [[:en:April 30|April 30]] - Matsugasaki Shrine festival ** [[:en:April 30|April 30]] - Flower Offering festival ** [[:en:May 1|May 1]] - Keishin Women's Association Spring Grand festival ** [[:en:May 1|May 1]] - Carp Memorial Service ** [[:en:May 2|May 2]] - Tea Offering festival ** [[:en:May 3|May 3]] - Mikoshi Procession * Late May - Yozan Memorial festival (Rice Planting festival) * [[:en:June 30|June 30]] - Great Purification ceremony * [[:en:July 30|July 30]] - Fukutoku Inari Shrine festival * [[September 25]] - Keizan Memorial Service * Last Saturday and Sunday of September - Matsugasaki Shrine Autumn Grand festival * Last Saturday and Sunday of September - Kasuga Shrine festival * Early October - Harvest festival * [[:en:November 15|November 15]] - Shichi-Go-San Prayers * [[:en:November 23|November 23]] - New Grain Thanksgiving festival * [[:en:December 29|December 29]] - Old Talisman Burning ceremony * [[:en:December 31|December 31]] - Great Purification ceremony and New Year's Eve festival ==Cultural Properties== [[File:Bishamonten (Uesugi Jinja Yonezawa).jpg|thumb|130px|right|Statue of Bishamonten (Late Heian period)]] [[File:Haramaki armour of Uesugi Kenshin.jpg|thumb|Iroiro-odoshi Haramaki with helmet and sleeve attachments, including black lacquer armor chest (allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin)]] '''[[:en:Important Cultural Properties|Important Cultural Properties]]''' * Painted silk statue of Bishamonten * Purple damask golden mandala of the Two Realms * Painted silk statue of the Amida Triad (Koryo period, signed as Gen, second year of Zhida, 1309) (stolen in 1987) * Sword said to be made by Tomonari, with inscription on the front and the date of the third year of Kōan on the back * Sword with no inscription, with gold and silver inlay of Sanskrit characters and seven stars, with sheath decorated with the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac (allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin) * Sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Motoshige * Long sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Norikuni, with fittings * Long sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Katayama Ichimonji, with fittings * Long sword with no inscription, allegedly made by Katayama Ichimonji, with fittings * Spear inscribed "Made by Maeda" on December of the second year of Bunroku (10 items) * Iroiro-odoshi Haramaki with helmet and sleeve attachments, including black lacquer armor chest (allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin) * Garments allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin and Uesugi Kagekatsu (details provided later) * Light blue silk garment (allegedly used by Naoe Kanetsugu) * Collection of sutras including Wheel Mandala Box * Dark blue paper with gold characters of the Heart Sutra written by Emperor Go-Nara (stolen in 1987) * Sword signed "Sukemune," with leather-bound handle, used by Uesugi Kagekatsu (owned by Matsugasaki Shrine) * Ming court gifts to Uesugi Kagekatsu (1 hanging scroll) and Ming court garments (Sha Mao (expanded angle), rhinoceros horn belt, large red thread chestplate, green lining, shoes) These were split from the Important Cultural Properties "Garments allegedly used by Uesugi Kenshin and Uesugi Kagekatsu" in 2018 (Notification No. 206 of the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, October 31, 2018) '''Other Cultural Properties''' * Gold small-laced light blue armor with accompanying helmet (used by Naoe Kanetsugu, known as the "Love" helmet)
